metadata.Initiative / Programme: Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Bill 2026
metadata.Description: Legislation implementing the EU AI Act in Ireland, establishing the AI Office of Ireland (Oifig IS na hÉireann) as regulator.

summary: The Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Bill 2026 is an Irish government legislative initiative to implement the EU AI Act in Ireland. It establishes the AI Office of Ireland and sets out regulatory coordination, oversight and enforcement arrangements affecting AI providers, deployers and other relevant actors. Its emphasis is on accountability, protecting health, safety and fundamental rights, and supporting responsible innovation. The available descriptions present it as a regulatory measure, not a teaching programme, and do not specify learning activities or pedagogy.
pedagogicalSummary: The inspected pages describe the Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Bill 2026 as a technical measure to implement the EU AI Act, not as a teaching or training initiative. They do not specify a pedagogy, learning activities, or instructional support provided by the Bill. The linked AI Act information page notes that providers and deployers must ensure staff have sufficient AI literacy, and points to an introductory course, but does not explain how the Bill organizes or teaches that learning. This is missing evidence about pedagogy, rather than evidence that AI-literacy teaching is absent elsewhere. (https://www.gov.ie/en/department-of-enterprise-tourism-and-employment/press-releases/publication-of-the-regulation-of-artificial-intelligence-bill-2026/; https://www.gov.ie/en/department-of-enterprise-tourism-and-employment/publications/eu-artificial-intelligence-ai-act/)
prioritySummary: The Bill principally establishes Ireland’s domestic enforcement and coordination arrangements for the EU AI Act, including an independent AI Office and powers for competent authorities. The stated aims combine protection of people’s health, safety and fundamental rights with oversight and accountability, while promoting trustworthy, human-centric AI and responsible innovation and adoption. The pages also describe a strategic interest in capturing AI’s economic and innovation opportunities, but frame this alongside regulatory safeguards rather than as a workforce-training initiative. These are policy goals, not evidence of an educational programme’s target learners. (https://www.gov.ie/en/department-of-enterprise-tourism-and-employment/press-releases/publication-of-the-regulation-of-artificial-intelligence-bill-2026/; https://www.gov.ie/en/department-of-enterprise-tourism-and-employment/publications/eu-artificial-intelligence-ai-act/)
educationalTechnologySummary: The inspected pages do not identify an educational technology developed or used by the Bill initiative to teach AI literacy. The linked government information page describes the European Commission’s AI Act Service Desk as an online information platform with interactive tools, including a Compliance Checker, to help stakeholders understand obligations; it is an external compliance resource, not identified as a learning technology used by the Bill. That page also mentions an “Introduction to AI” course from CeADAR, but the inspected material does not establish that the Bill develops, operates, or uses the course. Accordingly, evidence for educational technology attributable to the initiative is absent from the pages reviewed. (https://www.gov.ie/en/department-of-enterprise-tourism-and-employment/press-releases/publication-of-the-regulation-of-artificial-intelligence-bill-2026/; https://www.gov.ie/en/department-of-enterprise-tourism-and-employment/publications/eu-artificial-intelligence-ai-act/)

inclusion.reason: The initiative is issued by a national government (the Department of Enterprise, Tourism and Employment in Ireland), satisfying the government inclusion route. Additionally, it serves an educational function by establishing a regulatory framework that provides citizens and developers with information on how AI systems are governed, their risk levels, legal obligations, and compliance requirements, meeting the AI-literacy requirement.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: SOLAS micro-credential courses on AI for educators
metadata.Description: SOLAS-led further education and training micro-qualifications in AI (QQI-accredited, Levels 5–6) delivered via the 16 ETBs.

summary: SOLAS’s Skills to Advance programme offers QQI-accredited AI micro-qualifications for employees and employers in Ireland, delivered through the country’s 16 Education and Training Boards. The workplace-focused courses cover foundational AI concepts, data use, societal and ethical impacts, and practical generative AI skills such as prompt crafting and evaluating tools. Higher-level learning includes responsible and legally informed AI adoption, risk management, and strategic planning. Courses may be delivered in person, online, or in blended formats; specific teaching methods are not detailed.
pedagogicalSummary: The accessible course descriptions point to applied, work-oriented learning rather than a detailed account of teaching methods. The introductory course combines foundational AI concepts, ethical considerations, data use, and identifying applications for real-world problems. The Level 5 course connects GenAI principles to practice through prompt crafting, producing content, and evaluating tools’ suitability, limitations, effects, and ethical implications in professional contexts. The page says courses may be delivered in person, online, or in blended formats, but does not explain specific teaching activities, assessment, or how learning is supported in each format. These are stated learning outcomes and delivery options, not evidence of a particular pedagogy. (https://www.solas.ie/programmes/skills-to-advance/ai-micro-qualifications/)
prioritySummary: The initiative principally emphasizes building employees’ and employers’ capacity to adapt to AI-related workplace change. Its stated aims include improving digital capability, applying AI to everyday and professional tasks, and helping workers progress in their roles or adapt to a changing job market. Employer-facing benefits include strengthening teams and supporting a future-focused workforce, while employee-facing benefits include problem-solving and productivity. The Level 6 course description also emphasizes responsible, legally informed and strategic organisational adoption, including risk management and workforce engagement. The broader Skills to Advance initiative targets employees in changing jobs or vulnerable sectors and works with SMEs; the pages do not establish that AI literacy is aimed specifically at educators. (https://www.solas.ie/programmes/skills-to-advance/ai-micro-qualifications/; https://www.solas.ie/programmes/skills-to-advance/)
educationalTechnologySummary: The inspected pages do not identify a learning management system, instructional software, or hardware developed or used by SOLAS or the ETBs to teach these courses. They describe AI applications and GenAI tools as course content: learners are expected to identify and use applications, create content with GenAI tools, and practise prompt crafting. These are tools learners study or may use in professional practice, not evidence of a specific educational platform supplied by the initiative. A testimonial mentions a participant implementing a work system using Claude after training, but does not say Claude was used for instruction. metadata.Initiative / Programme: State Examinations Commission / NCCA guidance on AI in coursework
metadata.Description: SEC guidance on use, acknowledgement and authentication of AI in coursework.

summary: The State Examinations Commission (SEC) is Ireland’s statutory examinations authority. Its guidance addresses the use and acknowledgement of AI in coursework and how teachers can authenticate students’ work, supporting students and schools involved in state examinations. The initiative’s emphasis is assessment rules and submission procedures rather than a documented AI-literacy teaching programme; the available evidence does not establish a specific instructional approach.
pedagogicalSummary: The inspected pages present the State Examinations Commission primarily as an examinations and assessment authority, not as an AI-literacy teaching programme. They show digital coursework booklets for Leaving Certificate subjects and related submission information, but do not describe a teaching sequence, learner activities about AI, or a particular instructional approach. The available evidence therefore supports no specific AI-literacy pedagogy; this is a limit of the pages inspected, not confirmation that no further guidance exists. (https://www.examinations.ie/; https://www.examinations.ie/?l=en&mc=ex&sc=dcw)
prioritySummary: The SEC’s stated institutional role is the development, assessment, accreditation and certification of Ireland’s second-level examinations. Its digital-coursework information focuses on coursework booklets, completion and submission arrangements for candidates and schools. This points to administering and supporting state assessment as the evident emphasis, rather than a documented programme to build AI skills for a particular group or pursue a broader social-benefit goal. Although the initiative description refers to AI use, acknowledgement and authentication in coursework, the inspected pages did not provide the underlying AI guidance, so its specific aims and priorities cannot be established here. (https://www.examinations.ie/; https://www.examinations.ie/?l=en&mc=ex&sc=dcw)
educationalTechnologySummary: The inspected pages identify digital coursework booklets, some offered as Google Docs, and a Schools Portal with a user guide and an upload-instruction video; completed booklets are to be converted to PDF for submission. These are digital formats and assessment-submission supports, not evidence of an AI-literacy learning technology. The SEC also describes online services for examination results, appeals payments and external-candidate applications, but these are administrative services rather than tools shown supporting AI learning. No AI educational software, platform or hardware was identified in the pages inspected; this does not establish that none is addressed in uninspected guidance. (https://www.examinations.ie/?l=en&mc=ex&sc=dcw; https://www.examinations.ie/about-us/)

inclusion.reason: The SEC is a statutory body established by the State Examinations Act 1998 as part of the Irish government, providing national oversight of senior cycle examinations. Its guidance addresses how students should engage with AI (acknowledging its source) and how teachers must verify authentic student work, constituting educational content about responsible use of AI in academic contexts. As it is issued by a national statutory authority, it satisfies the inclusion route via government endorsement.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: AI Advisory Council recommendations "Helping to shape Ireland's AI future"
metadata.Description: Government-appointed council's February 2025 report recommending AI policy actions across six areas including AI literacy and education.

summary: The Irish Government-appointed AI Advisory Council’s February 2025 report, “Helping to shape Ireland’s AI future,” advises government on AI policy across six areas, including education and AI literacy, skills, responsible use, and infrastructure. For education, it recommends educator training through professional development, curriculum guidance, critical and constructive use of generative AI, equitable access to suitable tools, and monitoring effects on learning. These are policy proposals, not training, classroom activities, or technologies delivered by the Council; the report is principally aimed at policymakers.
pedagogicalSummary: This is a policy-advisory initiative, not a documented teaching programme. Its education paper recommends government-led AI-literacy training for educators at all levels, incorporated into professional development so teachers can build foundational knowledge and pass it on. It also advocates constructive use of generative AI alongside critical thinking about its capabilities and limitations, coordinated and regularly updated guidance, and monitoring of effects on student learning. These are proposed approaches rather than evidence of training or classroom activities implemented by the Council. The inspected material does not specify a detailed instructional method or curriculum. Sources: https://www.gov.ie/en/department-of-enterprise-tourism-and-employment/press-releases/irelands-ai-advisory-council-report-to-government-helping-to-shape-irelands-ai-future/ and https://assets.gov.ie/static/documents/ai-advisory-council-ai-and-education-paper.pdf
prioritySummary: The Council principally advises government on how Ireland can adopt and develop AI while managing risks. Its stated priorities span national competitiveness and economic growth, workforce preparedness for changing skills and jobs, responsible and ethical AI, and benefits for citizens and society. In education, it emphasizes AI literacy training for educators and equitable access to safe, private generative-AI tools for teachers and students, including attention to cost and Irish-language support. The inspected pages present these as recommendations, not as evidence that the Council itself delivers training or tools. They do not establish a single overriding beneficiary or a hierarchy between economic, workforce, educational, and societal aims. Sources: https://www.gov.ie/en/department-of-enterprise-tourism-and-employment/press-releases/irelands-ai-advisory-council-report-to-government-helping-to-shape-irelands-ai-future/ and https://assets.gov.ie/static/documents/ai-advisory-council-recommendations-helping-to-shape-irelands-ai-future.pdf
educationalTechnologySummary: The inspected pages do not identify an educational technology developed or operated by the AI Advisory Council. The Council recommends that government ensure equitable access to generative-AI tools in education, with tools that are free, private, secure, inclusive, and accessible to teachers and students; it does not name a particular product or platform or describe a rollout. Its education paper mentions examples of wider activity, including a University College Cork catalogue of generative-AI uses and the Learnovate Technology Centre, but does not present these as Council-developed or Council-used technologies. Generative AI is discussed as a possible teaching and learning tool, including for lesson preparation, tailored explanations, feedback, and accessibility support. These are potential uses, not evidence that the initiative provides them. Sources: https://assets.gov.ie/static/documents/ai-advisory-council-ai-and-education-paper.pdf and https://assets.gov.ie/static/documents/ai-advisory-council-recommendations-helping-to-shape-irelands-ai-future.pdf

inclusion.reason: The initiative qualifies under the inclusion route of being issued by a national government body (the Department of Enterprise, Tourism and Employment) through an officially established, multi-disciplinary council. The report directly addresses AI literacy as one of its six recommended focus areas and proposes concrete educational policy actions. Although the recommendations themselves are advisory rather than fully enacted legislation, the screening criteria allow inclusion for formally endorsed initiatives where government involvement is clear and the initiative’s core purpose includes AI literacy.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: ETBI AI Policy and Guidance Framework
metadata.Description: ETBI resource outlining policy considerations for responsible generative AI use across Ireland's 16 Education and Training Boards.

summary: Education and Training Boards Ireland (ETBI) provides a policy and guidance framework to help Ireland’s 16 Education and Training Boards develop approaches to responsible generative AI use. Intended for institutional leaders, staff, and learners, it covers acceptable use, academic integrity and assessment, privacy and security, ethics, transparency, intellectual property, staff support, and learner awareness. The resource also suggests ways to use and critically evaluate AI in learning, but describes recommendations rather than a delivered training programme or confirmed implementation across the boards.
pedagogicalSummary: The inspected material is guidance rather than a description of a delivered course or teaching programme, so it does not establish a formal instructional model. It encourages learners to treat generative AI as a support for learning, not a substitute for their own effort, and to check outputs for accuracy. Suggested learning practices include evaluating AI-generated content for bias, using it to generate self-test flashcards or practice questions, and reflecting on or critiquing AI output. For educators, the resource recommends varied assessment, including staged submissions with feedback, discussions, peer review, presentations, and projects; it also suggests making interaction with AI itself an object of assessment. These are recommendations, not evidence that ETBI implements them. (https://library.etbi.ie/staff/ai/learners; https://library.etbi.ie/staff/ai/assessments; https://library.etbi.ie/staff/ai/policy)
prioritySummary: The principal emphasis in the policy outline is helping educational institutions establish acceptable, responsible rules for generative AI use. It highlights academic integrity, transparency and accountability, data privacy and security, ethical use, intellectual property, legal risk, and alignment with educational aims. The intended beneficiaries and participants are broad: the outline calls for staff, learners, and managers to be consulted and supported, and points to learner guidance, staff training, and student awareness. The wider library guide also presents possible learning enhancement and accessibility benefits, while cautioning about risks; the inspected pages do not establish a single priority beyond responsible educational use and governance. This is a policy resource, not evidence of a specific implementation across institutions. (https://library.etbi.ie/staff/ai/policy; https://library.etbi.ie/staff/ai; https://library.etbi.ie/staff/ai/uses)
educationalTechnologySummary: The inspected pages do not identify an AI-literacy platform, software, or hardware developed or adopted by ETBI for its own teaching. The policy page discusses generative AI tools in general and proposes institutional criteria for tool selection, access, and support. A separate library page provides a representative, explicitly non-endorsed directory of external tools, including ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, and Byte, alongside education-oriented examples such as Brisk, Eduaide.ai, and Jamworks; it does not confirm that ETBI uses them. Learner guidance describes possible uses of generative AI and related tools for activities such as practice quizzes, summaries, tutoring, accessibility support, and language practice, but these are examples, not evidence of deployment by the initiative. (https://library.etbi.ie/staff/ai/tools; https://library.etbi.ie/staff/ai/learners; https://library.etbi.ie/staff/ai/policy)

inclusion.reason: The initiative meets the inclusion criteria for two reasons: (1) it is issued/mandated by EBTI, a statutory body of sub-national government entities (the 16 Education and Training Boards of Ireland), satisfying the 'Issued...by a national or sub-national government or statutory body' route. (2) It contains clear AI literacy elements including an explanation of AI ('What is AI?'), discussion of limitations, ethics, responsible usage guidelines, assessment strategies, and training/awareness content for both staff and learners. The resource serves the entire Irish further education and training sector.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Oide Technology in Education resources
metadata.Description: Oide TiE provides teacher professional learning on digital technologies and AI.

summary: Oide Technology in Education is an Irish national support service for school leaders and teachers in primary and post-primary schools. It provides professional learning through school-based support, courses, workshops, webinars and other resources to help embed digital technologies in teaching, learning and assessment. Its materials include an AI for Leaders resource for primary schools, though the available evidence does not establish a broader AI-literacy programme or specific pedagogy for that resource.
pedagogicalSummary: Oide describes professional learning for teachers and school leaders through school-based support, face-to-face and online courses, workshops, seminars, webinars, projects and good-practice videos. Its materials are intended for both individual and school-led professional development. The inspected resources include an “AI for Leaders (Primary)” item, but the pages do not explain its teaching methods or show whether it uses a particular approach such as hands-on practice or collaborative inquiry. The stated aim of developing critically engaged, active student learners is a policy goal, not enough on its own to establish a specific pedagogy. Evidence is therefore clearest about the formats used to support educators, rather than the pedagogy of the AI-related learning itself. (https://oide.ie/digital-technology/home/; https://oide.ie/digital-technology/home/digital-technology/; https://oide.ie/digital-technology/home/digital-technology/professional-learning-materials/)
prioritySummary: The inspected pages present Oide Technology in Education principally as a professional-learning and school-support service for school leaders, teachers and schools in Ireland. Its emphasis is helping them embed digital technologies effectively in teaching, learning and assessment, including support for digital learning planning and school practice. The stated intended student benefit is developing competent, critically engaged, active learners who can participate in a digital world; the material also lists an “AI for Leaders (Primary)” resource, indicating some AI-related support. The evidence supports both educator capacity-building and improved learning opportunities for students, but does not establish a more specific AI-literacy priority or rank these aims. (https://oide.ie/digital-technology/home/; https://oide.ie/digital-technology/home/digital-technology/; https://oide.ie/digital-technology/home/digital-technology/professional-learning-materials/)
educationalTechnologySummary: The pages describe support for embedding digital technologies in school teaching, learning and assessment, and mention guidance on school infrastructure, devices and networking. They also point to DLplanning.ie for digital learning planning, Webwise.ie for internet-safety guidance, and Scoilnet.ie for learning materials; these are identified as supporting websites, but the inspected pages do not establish which technologies Oide developed or how any specific platform is used in instruction. Oide offers online courses and webinars and lists AI-related professional-learning material, but the pages inspected do not name a learning platform, AI application, or particular hardware used in those activities. Thus, evidence supports broad use and guidance around digital technology, while details of specific educational technologies and their learning functions remain unavailable. (https://oide.ie/digital-technology/home/; https://oide.ie/digital-technology/home/digital-technology/professional-learning-materials/)

inclusion.reason: The initiative qualifies for inclusion via the government mandate inclusion route: Oide is a national support service operating under the aegis of the Department of Education and Skills (a national government body), with explicit mention that its previous functions were held by the National Centre for Technology in Education (NCTE) before integration into the Professional Development Service for Teachers (PDST) within the Department. The initiative explicitly focuses on empowering schools to harness digital transformation, develop digital competence, and includes content on AI as stated in the metadata provided. It serves Primary and Post-Primary schools nationwide, meeting the scale requirements.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Teaching Council Céim – Standards for Initial Teacher Education
metadata.Description: Standards for initial teacher education programmes incl. digital technologies.

summary: Céim is the Teaching Council of Ireland’s standards framework for initial teacher education programmes leading to teacher registration. It guides teacher-education providers and student teachers across undergraduate and postgraduate preparation for primary, post-primary and further education. The standards include requirements relating to digital and emerging technologies, alongside professional preparation such as supported school placement and inclusive-education experience. Its main emphasis is accreditation and preparation for entry to teaching, rather than AI literacy specifically.
pedagogicalSummary: Céim is presented as a set of standards for initial teacher education programmes, applied through the Teaching Council’s professional accreditation of programmes leading to teacher registration. The inspected page does not describe specific classroom teaching methods or a complete learning design. It does identify school placement as a critical part of initial teacher education: student teachers experience teaching and learning in varied contexts and participate in school life in a structured, supported way. It also describes an assessed, two-week special-education placement intended to build understanding of inclusive education and readiness to support pupils with significant needs. These are the clearest pedagogical details available on the inspected page; further approaches may be specified in the linked standards, which were not reviewed. (https://www.teachingcouncil.ie/professional-learning/initial-teacher-education/)
prioritySummary: The initiative’s principal emphasis is setting and accrediting standards for initial teacher education in Ireland, so programmes prepare people for entry to the teaching profession and meet requirements for registration. Its intended direct beneficiaries are student teachers and teacher-education providers, while the Council situates its wider regulatory role as protecting the public and promoting professional standards. The page covers primary, post-primary, and further-education teacher education, and describes school placement and inclusive-education experience as elements of preparation. The inspected material does not establish a distinct AI-literacy priority or identify workforce upskilling beyond preparing new teachers for professional entry. These conclusions reflect the public overview; the detailed standards were not inspected. (https://www.teachingcouncil.ie/professional-learning/initial-teacher-education/; https://www.teachingcouncil.ie/)
educationalTechnologySummary: The inspected Teaching Council pages identify Céim as standards for initial teacher education and describe accreditation, school placement, and an assessed placement for learning about inclusive education. They do not name a digital-learning platform, software, hardware, AI tool, or other educational technology developed or used to support learning. The initial-teacher-education page links to the Céim standards PDF, but the available page text does not describe the standards’ technology provisions, and the linked document was not reviewed. Accordingly, the inspected evidence is insufficient to say whether particular educational technologies are required or used; this is a limit of the inspection, not confirmation that none are used. (https://www.teachingcouncil.ie/professional-learning/initial-teacher-education/)

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Linee guida per l'introduzione dell'IA nelle istituzioni scolastiche (MIM, DM 166/2025)
metadata.Description: MIM guidelines (Aug 2025) for responsible AI introduction in schools, addressing leaders, staff, teachers and students.

summary: Italy’s Ministry of Education guidelines (DM 166/2025) set out an approach to introducing AI in school institutions, addressing school leaders, staff, teachers and students. They emphasize AI literacy and responsible use, including understanding AI, ethical considerations, transparency and explainability, human oversight, data protection, security and sustainability. The document is policy guidance rather than a documented teaching programme; the available evidence does not establish a specific pedagogy or particular educational technologies.
pedagogicalSummary: The accessible PDF identifies itself as 2025 guidelines for introducing artificial intelligence in schools, rather than describing a teaching programme. The readable portion does not establish a pedagogical approach, such as project-based learning, teacher-led instruction, or student activities; the table of contents is only partially visible in the returned text. This is missing evidence from the limited inspection, not confirmation that the full guidelines contain no pedagogical recommendations. Source: https://www.mim.gov.it/documents/20182/0/MIM_Linee+guida+IA+nella+Scuola_09_08_2025-signed.pdf/b70fdc45-4b75-1f7e-73bf-eab12989b928
prioritySummary: The document’s stated purpose is to guide the introduction of AI in Italian school institutions. This indicates an emphasis on supporting schools in adopting AI, with school communities as the apparent beneficiaries; the accessible text does not clarify whether the principal intended benefit is for students, teachers, school leaders, or society more broadly, nor does it establish a hierarchy among them. More specific goals cannot be reliably inferred from the cover and partial contents available in this inspection. Source: https://www.mim.gov.it/documents/20182/0/MIM_Linee+guida+IA+nella+Scuola_09_08_2025-signed.pdf/b70fdc45-4b75-1f7e-73bf-eab12989b928
educationalTechnologySummary: The accessible portion names artificial intelligence as the subject of the guidelines but does not identify any particular educational technology, platform, software, hardware, or AI tool developed or used by the initiative to support learning. The document is itself a policy-guidance PDF; its existence does not establish the use of an educational technology. Because the PDF’s substantive pages were not available in readable detail in this limited inspection, it is not possible to determine whether later sections name tools or systems. Source: https://www.mim.gov.it/documents/20182/0/MIM_Linee+guida+IA+nella+Scuola_09_08_2025-signed.pdf/b70fdc45-4b75-1f7e-73bf-eab12989b928

inclusion.reason: The initiative qualifies for inclusion under both the AI-literacy requirement and the national government endorsement route. The document is issued by the Italian Ministry of Education (MIM), a national statutory body, explicitly meeting the 'Issued... by a national or sub-national government' inclusion route. It contains clear educational content on how to use AI responsibly, principles of transparency and explainability, human-in-the-loop requirements, privacy compliance, and ethical considerations—constituting substantive AI literacy guidance. The document serves schools across Italy as official state guidelines.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Strategia Italiana per l'Intelligenza Artificiale 2024–2026
metadata.Description: Italian government AI strategy covering research, public administration, business and training strategy pillars.

summary: Italy’s 2024–2026 national AI strategy sets priorities for research, public administration, enterprises and training. It is aimed at public-sector decision-makers, researchers, businesses and people involved in AI training, with a broad emphasis on developing and adopting AI across these areas. Training is one of the strategy’s four main areas, but the available evidence does not specify its teaching methods or supporting technologies.
pedagogicalSummary: The accessible PDF identifies a strategy for training as one of its sections, alongside strategies for research, public administration and enterprises, but the inspected text does not reveal what training involves or how it is taught. It therefore does not support identifying a particular pedagogy, such as project-based learning, formal courses or peer learning. This is a gap in the accessible evidence, not confirmation that the full strategy contains no teaching approaches. Source: https://www.agid.gov.it/sites/agid/files/2024-07/Strategia_italiana_per_l_Intelligenza_artificiale_2024-2026.pdf
prioritySummary: The document is a national AI strategy, and its contents list distinct strategy areas for research, public administration, enterprises and training. These indicate a broad agenda spanning AI research and adoption across public and business settings, as well as training; the accessible text does not establish a single overriding priority, intended beneficiary hierarchy, or specific AI-literacy objective. Because only the cover and contents were readable in the inspection, more detailed goals and the relative weight given to these areas remain uncertain. Source: https://www.agid.gov.it/sites/agid/files/2024-07/Strategia_italiana_per_l_Intelligenza_artificiale_2024-2026.pdf
educationalTechnologySummary: The accessible portion of the strategy does not identify educational technologies, platforms, software or hardware used or developed to support learning. It names a strategy for training as a policy area, but that alone does not establish which tools, if any, support it. The PDF itself is a strategy document, not evidence of an educational technology. This finding reflects the limited inspection: the document’s substantive pages could not be read in the available extraction, so it would be unwarranted to conclude that no technologies are discussed elsewhere in the strategy. Source: https://www.agid.gov.it/sites/agid/files/2024-07/Strategia_italiana_per_l_Intelligenza_artificiale_2024-2026.pdf

inclusion.reason: The initiative includes extensive educational and training strategy elements (specifically mentioned in the title and content), providing AI literacy guidance. It is formally endorsed by a national government (Italy) as indicated by the source domain (agid.gov.it) and official metadata, satisfying the government endorsement inclusion route.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Law 132/2025 on Artificial Intelligence
metadata.Description: Italian framework law on AI (Legge 23 settembre 2025, n. 132), incl. provisions on AI literacy and training.

summary: Italy’s Law 132/2025 establishes a national framework for AI research, development, adoption and use, with provisions on governance, rights, safety and sector-specific applications. Within this broader regulatory framework, it calls for AI training for workers and employers, judicial and administrative personnel, and capacity-building in public administrations. The provisions emphasize responsible use, relevant digital and transversal skills, and awareness of AI’s benefits and risks, but do not specify a common curriculum, course format or teaching technology.
pedagogicalSummary: Law 132/2025 is principally a regulatory framework, not a described teaching programme. It does, however, direct the Justice Minister to promote didactic activities for magistrates on AI and its judicial uses, covering basic and advanced digital skills, sharing competencies, and awareness of benefits and risks; administrative staff are also to be trained. The law also calls for worker and employer training, and for public administrations to take formative measures that support responsible AI use and users’ transversal skills. These provisions identify audiences and learning aims, but the inspected text does not specify teaching methods, course formats, or a common curriculum. Evidence: https://www.gazzettaufficiale.it/atto/serie_generale/caricaArticolo?art.versione=1&art.idGruppo=2&art.flagTipoArticolo=0&art.codiceRedazionale=25G00143&art.idArticolo=15&art.idSottoArticolo=1&art.idSottoArticolo1=10&art.dataPubblicazioneGazzetta=2025-09-25&art.progressivo=0 ; https://www.gazzettaufficiale.it/atto/serie_generale/caricaArticolo?art.versione=1&art.idGruppo=2&art.flagTipoArticolo=0&art.codiceRedazionale=25G00143&art.idArticolo=12&art.idSottoArticolo=1&art.idSottoArticolo1=10&art.dataPubblicazioneGazzetta=2025-09-25&art.progressivo=0 ; https://www.gazzettaufficiale.it/atto/serie_generale/caricaArticolo?art.versione=1&art.idGruppo=2&art.flagTipoArticolo=0&art.codiceRedazionale=25G00143&art.idArticolo=14&art.idSottoArticolo=1&art.idSottoArticolo1=10&art.dataPubblicazioneGazzetta=2025-09-25&art.progressivo=0
prioritySummary: The law’s central purpose is to establish principles and governance for AI research, development, adoption, and use in Italy, encouraging its opportunities while requiring responsible, transparent, human-centred use and oversight of risks to rights and society. Its priorities span several beneficiaries rather than one declared dominant group: it promotes AI-related knowledge and research, business and industrial innovation and competitiveness, and public-sector capacity and services. It also addresses workers’ conditions and training, and professional and judicial users’ understanding of AI. The inspected provisions do not set out a single AI-literacy initiative or rank these aims; literacy and training appear as elements within a broader national framework. Evidence: https://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:legge:2025-09-23;132 ; https://www.gazzettaufficiale.it/atto/serie_generale/caricaArticolo?art.versione=1&art.idGruppo=3&art.flagTipoArticolo=0&art.codiceRedazionale=25G00143&art.idArticolo=19&art.idSottoArticolo=1&art.idSottoArticolo1=10&art.dataPubblicazioneGazzetta=2025-09-25&art.progressivo=0 ; https://www.gazzettaufficiale.it/atto/serie_generale/caricaArticolo?art.versione=1&art.idGruppo=2&art.flagTipoArticolo=0&art.codiceRedazionale=25G00143&art.idArticolo=11&art.idSottoArticolo=1&art.idSottoArticolo1=10&art.dataPubblicazioneGazzetta=2025-09-25&art.progressivo=0
educationalTechnologySummary: The inspected law does not identify a learning platform, educational software, hardware, or AI tool used or developed to teach AI literacy. It does establish an AI platform designed, operated, and owned by AGENAS to support healthcare professionals and users with care-related services, including non-binding suggestions; the stated purpose is healthcare support, not learning, so it is not evidence of an educational technology for AI literacy. The law’s references to AI systems in public administration, work, and judicial activity likewise concern their application in those settings rather than teaching tools. This summary is limited to the inspected provisions, and does not establish that no such tools exist elsewhere. Evidence: https://www.gazzettaufficiale.it/atto/serie_generale/caricaArticolo?art.versione=1&art.idGruppo=2&art.flagTipoArticolo=0&art.codiceRedazionale=25G00143&art.idArticolo=10&art.idSottoArticolo=1&art.idSottoArticolo1=10&art.dataPubblicazioneGazzetta=2025-09-25&art.progressivo=0 ; https://www.normattiva.it/uri-res/N2Ls?urn:nir:stato:legge:2025-09-23;132

metadata.Initiative / Programme: PNRR education investments (e.g. Piano Scuola 4.0)
metadata.Description: Recovery plan investments in digital learning environments and labs.

summary: Italy’s Ministry of Education PNRR education investments support schools and other education providers through classroom and laboratory modernization, digital-learning infrastructure, staff training, and initiatives in STEM, languages, and skills for work. Scuola 4.0 promotes connected, flexible learning environments, while Scuola Futura provides professional-development courses. AI appears within broader digital-skills goals and in some reported school activities and events; the available evidence does not establish a consistent AI-literacy curriculum across the programme.
pedagogicalSummary: The inspected pages describe a broad mix of approaches rather than a single AI-literacy teaching method. The School 4.0 investment aims to move beyond lecture-oriented classrooms toward connected, hybrid physical-and-digital learning environments and to support changes in teaching and learning methods. A school example describes practical, interdisciplinary and immersive learning using modernized laboratories and AI-based visors; another describes an AI-focused teacher-training lesson at the Herculaneum archaeological site, using a future scenario to prompt participants to rethink teaching. The broader program also provides staff training through courses and local training hubs. These examples indicate experiential, hands-on and interdisciplinary approaches, but the pages do not establish that they are used consistently across schools or specify a standard AI-literacy curriculum. Sources: https://pnrr.istruzione.it/infrastrutture/scuole-4-0-nuove-aule-didattiche-e-laboratori/ ; https://pnrr.istruzione.it/storie/scuola-4-0-al-liceo-montale-di-roma-nuovi-laboratori-smart-board-e-ia/ ; https://pnrr.istruzione.it/storie/storia-archeologia-e-intelligenza-artificiale-nei-percorsi-formativi-del-pantaleo/
prioritySummary: The initiative’s documented emphasis is broad transformation of Italian education, not AI literacy alone. School 4.0 seeks to modernize classrooms and laboratories with connected digital learning environments, develop digital skills relevant to future work—including in digitalization and AI—and train school staff for the digital transition. Other measures aim to improve students’ STEM and computer-science learning, address gender equality and equal opportunity, and reduce territorial learning gaps and school dropout through tailored support, mentoring and guidance. The pages set out these goals for schools, students and school personnel, but do not establish one as the overriding priority across the entire PNRR education program. AI appears as one part of digital skills and in examples of school activity, rather than as the sole or principal stated objective. Sources: https://pnrr.istruzione.it/infrastrutture/scuole-4-0-nuove-aule-didattiche-e-laboratori/ ; https://pnrr.istruzione.it/competenze/didattica-digitale-integrata-e-formazione-sulla-transizione-digitale-del-personale-scolastico/ ; https://pnrr.istruzione.it/competenze/nuove-competenze-e-nuovi-linguaggi/ ; https://pnrr.istruzione.it/competenze/riduzione-dei-divari-territoriali/
educationalTechnologySummary: The pages identify both a training platform and school-based equipment. Scuola Futura is a named platform where school personnel can find training courses, enrol, participate and receive certificates; the investment description also envisages a platform with digital-education content and innovative teaching methods. School 4.0 funding supports connected digital classrooms and upgraded laboratories. A cited school example reports smart boards, improved network infrastructure, modernized laboratory equipment and AI-based visors, which support practical and immersive learning; these are examples from one school, not a standardized inventory. The site does not name specific AI software or identify a particular AI tool developed by the initiative. Scuola Futura is described as a platform used for professional learning, while the classroom technologies are acquired or installed by schools. Sources: https://pnrr.istruzione.it/competenze/didattica-digitale-integrata-e-formazione-sulla-transizione-digitale-del-personale-scolastico/ ; https://scuolafutura.pubblica.istruzione.it/ ; https://pnrr.istruzione.it/infrastrutture/scuole-4-0-nuove-aule-didattiche-e-laboratori/ ; https://pnrr.istruzione.it/storie/scuola-4-0-al-liceo-montale-di-roma-nuovi-laboratori-smart-board-e-ia/

inclusion.reason: The initiative is officially issued/endorsed by the Italian Ministry of Education under the EU-funded PNRR, satisfying an inclusion route (government endorsement/funding). The site references AI-related events and investments but does not yet display explicit educational content on how AI works or to use it; however, missing evidence of AI-literacy elements does not warrant exclusion. Include with uncertainty about current AI-literacy content availability.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Linee guida per l'insegnamento dell'educazione civica (2024)
metadata.Description: MIM guidelines (Sept 2024) updating civic education teaching objectives, including digital citizenship elements.

summary: Italy’s Ministry of Education and Merit’s 2024 civic-education guidelines set learning objectives for schools’ civic-education curricula from the 2024/25 school year, covering the Constitution, economic development and sustainability, and digital citizenship. They apply across the first and second school cycles, with awareness-raising activities for preschool. Within digital citizenship, the guidelines address AI and its responsible use, critical assessment of digital information and data, privacy, and cyberbullying prevention. They provide a national curriculum framework rather than prescribing specific teaching methods; implementation is left to schools’ curricula and educational plans.
pedagogicalSummary: The initiative sets a national curriculum framework rather than prescribing a specific classroom method in the accessible material. The 2024 decree says the guidelines define competency-development targets and learning objectives for the first and second school cycles, and awareness-raising actions for preschool; schools are to update their civic-education curricula and three-year educational plans accordingly. The decree also refers to flexibility in schools’ organization of teaching, but the inspected pages do not establish particular methods such as project-based learning, discussion, or practical exercises. Thus, the evidence supports nationally defined learning outcomes implemented through school curricula, while details of teaching practice remain unclear. Sources: https://www.istruzione.it/educazione_civica/index.html and https://www.miur.gov.it/documents/20182/0/Decreto+(1).pdf/4a35f2a3-4b53-6e9d-a0eb-a3d6ad4c9134?t=1725710176010
prioritySummary: The stated emphasis is preparing responsible citizens through school civic education. The Ministry’s overview describes the initiative as a path to form responsible citizens and identifies three strands: the Constitution, economic development and sustainability, and digital citizenship. The guidelines apply to national-school-system curricula from the 2024/25 school year; the decree specifies learning objectives for the first and second cycles and awareness-raising for preschool. The evidence therefore indicates a broad civic and educational purpose, including digital citizenship, rather than a narrowly workforce-focused or individual well-being initiative. The inspected overview does not provide enough detail to rank the three strands or identify a more specific beneficiary priority. Sources: https://www.istruzione.it/educazione_civica/index.html and https://www.miur.gov.it/documents/20182/0/Decreto+(1).pdf/4a35f2a3-4b53-6e9d-a0eb-a3d6ad4c9134?t=1725710176010
educationalTechnologySummary: The inspected material does not identify a learning platform, software, hardware, or other educational technology developed or used by the initiative. The overview lists digital citizenship as one of the civic-education strands, and the decree mentions digital technologies in the context of managing money; these are learning topics, not evidence that a specific technology supports instruction. The initiative appears in the accessible sources as ministerial guidelines and a framework for schools’ curricula, not as a technology product or delivery platform. Because the full guidelines PDF could not be inspected beyond its opening preview, this is a limit of the available evidence, not confirmation that schools use no digital tools in teaching. Sources: https://www.istruzione.it/educazione_civica/index.html and https://www.miur.gov.it/documents/20182/0/Decreto+(1).pdf/4a35f2a3-4b53-6e9d-a0eb-a3d6ad4c9134?t=1725710176010

metadata.Initiative / Programme: MIM pilot of AI virtual assistants/tutors in classes (4 regions)
metadata.Description: Two-year MIM pilot (15 classes, 4 regions: Lombardia, Toscana, Lazio, Calabria) testing AI virtual assistants to flag student learning difficulties.

summary: An Italian Ministry of Education two-year pilot will test AI virtual assistants in 15 classes across four regions. Initially focused on STEM subjects and foreign languages, the software is intended to identify individual students’ learning gaps, alert students and teachers, and suggest ways to address them; teachers provide the targeted support. The pilot includes teacher training and is intended to support students facing learning difficulties, with INVALSI set to evaluate results. The accompanying report also discusses responsible, legal and ethical use of AI in schools.
pedagogicalSummary: The reported approach is individualized, diagnostic support within teacher-led instruction, rather than a described programme for teaching AI literacy itself. The virtual assistant is intended to identify an individual student’s learning gaps, alert the student and teacher, and suggest a way to address them; a trained teacher then provides targeted help. The article says the model is inspired by Benjamin S. Bloom’s work on the benefits of sustained individual support, while stressing that the AI is supplementary and does not replace teachers. It does not describe specific classroom lesson formats or how students learn to understand AI. Evidence is limited to this report of a planned pilot: https://www.orizzontescuola.it/lintelligenza-artificiale-sbarca-a-scuola-15-classi-4-regioni-pilota-ecco-come-funzionera-la-sperimentazione-se-andra-bene-a-regime-nel-2026/
prioritySummary: The pilot is principally presented as a way to improve student learning and equity: it aims to narrow learning gaps, with particular attention to students experiencing difficulty and students of foreign origin. The article also identifies two broader aims—supporting social mobility by enabling students to improve regardless of their starting circumstances, and reducing school dropout, especially around the choice of upper-secondary school. These are stated aims of the proposed pilot, not outcomes established by the article; results were to be evaluated after two years by INVALSI. The report does not frame workforce upskilling or AI literacy as the principal priority. Source: https://www.orizzontescuola.it/lintelligenza-artificiale-sbarca-a-scuola-15-classi-4-regioni-pilota-ecco-come-funzionera-la-sperimentazione-se-andra-bene-a-regime-nel-2026/
educationalTechnologySummary: The article describes a planned virtual assistant powered by AI, delivered through software installable on Google Workspace. The pilot is initially to focus on STEM subjects and foreign languages. The assistant is intended to detect individual learning difficulties, notify both student and teacher, and suggest ways for the student to address a gap; the teacher remains responsible for intervention. Google Workspace is identified as the software environment, but the article gives no product or assistant name and does not say that the initiative developed the software. It reports planned use, not evaluated classroom results, and provides no further details about devices, system design, or other learning technologies. Source: https://www.orizzontescuola.it/lintelligenza-artificiale-sbarca-a-scuola-15-classi-4-regioni-pilota-ecco-come-funzionera-la-sperimentazione-se-andra-bene-a-regime-nel-2026/

inclusion.reason: The initiative qualifies for inclusion as it is a government-endorsed educational pilot (involving multiple Italian regions and the school system) that addresses AI literacy. The site provides specific educational guidance on 'how to use' these AI tools, covering ethical use, legal responsibilities for teachers, practical tips for integrating them into classrooms, and strategies to avoid pitfalls without relying solely on technology. This meets the requirement of including AI literacy content within a project endorsed by government bodies (regions/ministry level) with clear educational objectives rather than just product promotion or simple tool usage.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Nuove Indicazioni nazionali (curriculum guidelines, first cycle 2025)
metadata.Description: New national curriculum guidelines (Dec 2025) introducing explicit computer science and initial AI familiarisation from primary school.

summary: Italy’s national curriculum guidelines for early-childhood education and the first cycle of schooling provide a policy framework for educators and learners across these stages. Alongside computational skills such as algorithm design and robotics, they introduce familiarity with AI, including awareness of its social effects and responsible, safe use of AI tools. The available evidence establishes the curriculum’s scope and learning aims but not specific teaching methods or supporting technologies.
pedagogicalSummary: The accessible opening of the document identifies it as national curriculum guidelines for early-childhood education and the first cycle of schooling, but does not expose enough of the curriculum’s body to establish its teaching methods or how learning is supported. Thus, the inspected evidence confirms a curriculum-guidance framework, not a particular pedagogy; the approach to AI learning specifically remains unclear. Source: https://www.mim.gov.it/documents/20182/10554370/curricolo_web.pdf/f91c31a0-5ed4-65f3-bfea-fb49adaba55f?version=1.0&t=1773224873548
prioritySummary: The document’s title establishes its principal scope as national curriculum guidance for early-childhood education and the first cycle of schooling, so its evident beneficiaries are learners and educators in those stages. The accessible opening does not reveal the curriculum’s substantive aims or confirm whether AI literacy is a leading priority; that emphasis cannot be determined from the inspected text. Source: https://www.mim.gov.it/documents/20182/10554370/curricolo_web.pdf/f91c31a0-5ed4-65f3-bfea-fb49adaba55f?version=1.0&t=1773224873548
educationalTechnologySummary: No educational technologies, platforms, software, or hardware are identified in the accessible opening of the curriculum document. The document is identifiable as curriculum guidance, but the inspected text is insufficient to determine whether later sections prescribe or develop any tools for AI-literacy learning. This is a limit of the available evidence, not confirmation that the initiative uses or develops none. Source: https://www.mim.gov.it/documents/20182/10554370/curricolo_web.pdf/f91c31a0-5ed4-65f3-bfea-fb49adaba55f?version=1.0&t=1773224873548

inclusion.reason: The initiative includes AI literacy by defining explicit learning objectives for algorithmic thinking, robotics, and familiarity with AI in primary education. It qualifies under the 'Government Endorsement' inclusion route as it is an official document issued by a national government ministry (MIM).

metadata.Initiative / Programme: PNRR DM 66/2023 – teacher/staff training for the digital transition
metadata.Description: PNRR decree funding training of school staff on digital transition.

summary: Italy’s PNRR DM 66/2023 initiative funds continuing professional development for school staff, including teachers, school leaders, administrative managers, educational staff, and ATA personnel, to support the digital transition in teaching and school organization. Training is organized through local school hubs, with courses available through the Scuola Futura platform and skills development aligned with DigComp 2.2 and DigCompEdu. The national programme sets a target of training at least 650,000 staff and supports more than 8,000 educational institutions. Some related funded initiatives describe laboratory, co-design, and cooperative approaches, but these are not established as the format for every DM 66 course; the initiative’s emphasis is broad digital education rather than AI specifically.
pedagogicalSummary: The initiative organizes digital-transition learning as continuing professional development for school staff, delivered through local school training hubs and a national system; the broader investment also envisages a course catalogue spanning school subjects. Some funded national and international training initiatives explicitly use laboratory-based activities, co-design, cooperative learning, and project- and exploration-based approaches, with digital technologies used critically and consciously. These methods are stated for those initiatives, not established as the approach of every DM 66/2023 course. The inspected pages describe intended structures and methods but do not detail the day-to-day teaching format or assessment of DM 66 courses. (https://pnrr.istruzione.it/avviso/didattica-digitale-integrata/; https://pnrr.istruzione.it/avviso/didattica-digitale-integrata-e-formazione-alla-transizione-digitale-per-il-personale-scolastico/)
prioritySummary: The clearest priority is upskilling school staff for the digital transition in teaching and school organization. Under DM 66/2023, funding supports local training for school leaders, administrative managers, teachers, educational staff, and ATA staff, aligned with DigComp 2.2 and DigCompEdu; the stated national target is training at least 650,000 staff, with funding also intended to reach more than 8,000 educational institutions and 40% reserved for schools in southern regions. The wider investment links staff development to improved student learning and faster innovation across the school system. The inspected pages establish these workforce and system-level aims, but offer limited evidence about individual well-being as a separate priority. (https://pnrr.istruzione.it/avviso/didattica-digitale-integrata/; https://pnrr.istruzione.it/competenze/didattica-digitale-integrata-e-formazione-sulla-transizione-digitale-del-personale-scolastico/)
educationalTechnologySummary: The identified learning platform is Scuola Futura, which the initiative says staff can use to find courses, enroll, participate, and receive certificates. The broader investment also envisages a digital platform containing digital-education content and innovative teaching methodologies for teachers, students, and families. These are platforms supporting access to training and learning resources; the inspected pages do not name particular learning software, AI tools, or hardware developed or used in the courses. “Futura PNRR – Gestione Progetti” is mentioned for schools’ project applications, but the page presents it as project administration rather than a learning technology. Thus the evidence identifies a training platform and a planned educational-content platform, without enough detail to establish the specific tools used within courses. (https://pnrr.istruzione.it/competenze/didattica-digitale-integrata-e-formazione-sulla-transizione-digitale-del-personale-scolastico/; https://pnrr.istruzione.it/avviso/didattica-digitale-integrata/)

inclusion.reason: The initiative is mandated by a national government decree (DM 66/2022) and falls under Italy’s PNRR funding program. It explicitly includes training for school staff on the digital transition—i.e., educational content and learning objectives about using digital tools and AI in education. Because it is officially issued, funded, and managed by a national authority (Miur), it satisfies the inclusion route of government endorsement/funding. No exclusion criteria apply.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: PNRR teacher training on AI (DM 219/2025; €100m)
metadata.Description: MIM/PNRR decree (€100m) funding up to 2,000 schools to become AI training hubs for teacher digital/AI skills.

summary: Italy’s Ministry of Education, funded through the PNRR under DM 219/2025, supports up to 2,000 schools in establishing territorial hubs for training on digital transition and AI in schools. The initiative primarily targets teachers and other school staff, with projects that may also involve students. Planned activities include training courses, workshops and hands-on laboratories using AI devices and applications; schools apply through project proposals, potentially in consortia.
pedagogicalSummary: The notice describes training organised through territorial hubs, with courses and workshops for training and further exploration, alongside practical laboratories using AI devices and applications. It allows for student involvement, but does not specify whether this is routine or describe particular teaching methods, learning sequences, assessment, or support for learners. The accessible evidence therefore supports a mixed format of structured training and hands-on lab work, rather than a more detailed pedagogical model. These are learning activities, distinct from the initiative’s broader goal of digital transition. Evidence: https://pnrr.istruzione.it/news/avviso-pubblico-per-la-presentazione-di-proposte-progettuali-per-la-costituzione-di-snodi-formativi-per-la-transizione-digitale-sullutilizzo-dellintelligenza-artificiale-nella-scuola/.
prioritySummary: The initiative’s stated emphasis is building territorial training hubs to support digital transition through the use of AI in schools. The main direct beneficiaries appear to be school staff receiving training and professional development; the notice also says students may be involved in training projects, so benefits are not necessarily limited to staff. It does not describe workforce preparation outside education, individual well-being, or a wider societal outcome as its primary purpose. The inspected page establishes the focus on school-based AI use and training, but offers limited detail about how priorities are balanced or what outcomes are expected. Evidence: https://pnrr.istruzione.it/news/avviso-pubblico-per-la-presentazione-di-proposte-progettuali-per-la-costituzione-di-snodi-formativi-per-la-transizione-digitale-sullutilizzo-dellintelligenza-artificiale-nella-scuola/.
educationalTechnologySummary: The notice says the training projects may include laboratories using AI devices and applications, but does not name specific products, platforms, software, or hardware, nor explain how particular tools support learning. It presents these technologies as resources used in the training activities; the inspected page does not establish that the initiative develops them. The page also does not identify a dedicated learning platform for this particular call. Thus, evidence supports planned hands-on use of AI devices and applications, but not a more specific account of the educational technology ecosystem. Evidence: https://pnrr.istruzione.it/news/avviso-pubblico-per-la-presentazione-di-proposte-progettuali-per-la-costituzione-di-snodi-formativi-per-la-transizione-digitale-sullutilizzo-dellintelligenza-artificiale-nella-scuola/.

inclusion.reason: The initiative includes explicit AI literacy components through the goal of creating AI training hubs for developing teachers' digital and AI competencies, supported by DM 219/2025. It qualifies for inclusion via multiple routes: it is issued and funded by a national government body (Italian Ministry of Education and PNRR), has clear educational content focused on teacher AI skills, and targets thousands of schools with system-scale potential. No exclusion criteria apply.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Scuola Futura platform
metadata.Description: MIM platform for PNRR-funded staff training.

summary: Scuola Futura is an Italian Ministry of Education platform for professional development of in-service teachers and other school staff, supported by PNRR funding. Among its broader training pathways and resources, it offers AI-focused courses and materials addressing how AI works, responsible use, and implications for teaching, assessment, inclusion, and school management; some courses also help teachers foster pupils’ AI literacy. Course formats vary, with examples combining guided study, practical lesson or assessment design, exercises, and discussion. Materials in a DigComp 3.0 pathway include lesson plans, videos, audio overviews, infographics, and prompts.
pedagogicalSummary: Scuola Futura’s AI-literacy training uses a mix of structured instruction and applied work, though individual courses are organized by their providers and the inspected pages do not establish one uniform method. A course for teachers introducing AI to under-14s combines lessons, lesson design, exercises conducted independently or with a trainer, and a final session for sharing and discussion; it proposes playful, unplugged classroom activities. Another course uses critical reflection and a workshop in which teachers design a learning activity and consider assessment. The DigComp 3.0 course provides five theoretical modules with lesson plans, video tutorials, audio overviews, maps, infographics, and ready-to-use prompts. These examples support describing a blend of guided study, practical design, and reflection, not a platform-wide pedagogy. (https://scuolafutura.pubblica.istruzione.it/l-intelligenza-artificiale-spiegata-ai-pi%C3%B9-piccoli-percorsi-di-ai-literacy-under-14-class-experience-; https://scuolafutura.pubblica.istruzione.it/ia-come-cambiano-o-possono-cambiare-la-didattica-e-la-valutazione; https://scuolafutura.pubblica.istruzione.it/home/-/asset_publisher/6jrMqHc8bStK/content/a-scuola-con-il-quadro-europeo-digcomp-3.0-un-nuovo-percorso-di-formazione-su-scuola-futura?_com_liferay_asset_publisher_web_portlet_AssetPublisherPortlet_INSTANCE_6jrMqHc8bStK_assetEntryId=3472281&_com_liferay_asset_publisher_web_portlet_AssetPublisherPortlet_INSTANCE_6jrMqHc8bStK_redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fscuolafutura.pubblica.istruzione.it%2Fhome%3Fp_p_id%3Dcom_liferay_asset_publisher_web_portlet_AssetPublisherPortlet_INSTANCE_6jrMqHc8bStK%26p_p_lifecycle%3D0%26p_p_state%3Dnormal%26p_p_mode%3Dview%26_com_liferay_asset_publisher_web_portlet_AssetPublisherPortlet_INSTANCE_6jrMqHc8bStK_cur%3D0%26p_r_p_resetCur%3Dfalse%26_com_liferay_asset_publisher_web_portlet_AssetPublisherPortlet_INSTANCE_6jrMqHc8bStK_assetEntryId%3D3472281)
prioritySummary: The clearest emphasis is professional development for school staff, especially teachers and, in some courses, school leaders: the platform’s pathways are restricted to serving teachers and school personnel, and the AI courses aim to equip them to understand AI and address it in teaching, assessment, inclusion, and school management. A related intended benefit is students’ AI literacy. The under-14 course explicitly aims to help teachers move pupils from passive AI use toward critical, informed observation, including understanding how machines learn and their limitations while recognizing human empathy and creativity. Other listed aims include responsible and ethical integration, digital citizenship, and student data literacy. The inspected evidence supports these overlapping priorities, but not a single ranking across all platform offerings. (https://scuolafutura.pubblica.istruzione.it/percorsi; https://scuolafutura.pubblica.istruzione.it/l-intelligenza-artificiale-spiegata-ai-pi%C3%B9-piccoli-percorsi-di-ai-literacy-under-14-class-experience-; https://scuolafutura.pubblica.istruzione.it/web/scuola-futura/risorse/artificial-intelligence)
educationalTechnologySummary: The platform is used to list training, manage access and registrations, and provide details for online and in-person courses; the pages do not identify it as an AI-literacy teaching application. One teacher course proposes teacher-mediated, low-risk educational apps for pupils alongside unplugged activities, but names no apps. The DigComp 3.0 training materials include lesson plans, video tutorials, audio overviews, maps, infographics, and ready-to-use prompts. The AI resources page also describes related European projects: GenAI4Schools expects to develop an AI playbook and interaction models, while AI-DL involves co-creating teaching materials and experimenting with generative AI in education; AI4T provides a MOOC, synchronous training, and an open AI book. These are identified resources and project outputs, but the inspected pages do not establish that Scuola Futura itself develops or deploys a named AI learning tool. (https://scuolafutura.pubblica.istruzione.it/percorsi; https://scuolafutura.pubblica.istruzione.it/l-intelligenza-artificiale-spiegata-ai-pi%C3%B9-piccoli-percorsi-di-ai-literacy-under-14-class-experience-; https://scuolafutura.pubblica.istruzione.it/home/-/asset_publisher/6jrMqHc8bStK/content/a-scuola-con-il-quadro-europeo-digcomp-3.0-un-nuovo-percorso-di-formazione-su-scuola-futura?_com_liferay_asset_publisher_web_portlet_AssetPublisherPortlet_INSTANCE_6jrMqHc8bStK_assetEntryId=3472281&_com_liferay_asset_publisher_web_portlet_AssetPublisherPortlet_INSTANCE_6jrMqHc8bStK_redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fscuolafutura.pubblica.istruzione.it%2Fhome%3Fp_p_id%3Dcom_liferay_asset_publisher_web_portlet_AssetPublisherPortlet_INSTANCE_6jrMqHc8bStK%26p_p_lifecycle%3D0%26p_p_state%3Dnormal%26p_p_mode%3Dview%26_com_liferay_asset_publisher_web_portlet_AssetPublisherPortlet_INSTANCE_6jrMqHc8bStK_cur%3D0%26p_r_p_resetCur%3Dfalse%26_com_liferay_asset_publisher_web_portlet_AssetPublisherPortlet_INSTANCE_6jrMqHc8bStK_assetEntryId%3D3472281; https://scuolafutura.pubblica.istruzione.it/web/scuola-futura/risorse/artificial-intelligence)

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Agenda Digitale Italiana
metadata.Description: Italy's digital agenda (AgID).

summary: Agenda Digitale Italiana is the national digital-agenda initiative led by AgID, Italy’s public digital agency. Its AI work combines guidance for public administrations on adoption and safe use with training and learning resources for public officials, businesses, ICT and innovation organisations, academia, researchers and citizens. Through AgID Academy and AI events, it offers webinars, recordings and written materials on AI applications, public-sector use, regulation, responsibility and risks, supporting both live and asynchronous learning. The initiative also contributes to national AI policy and guidance; the available evidence does not establish a dedicated AI-learning platform or audience figures.
pedagogicalSummary: AgID Academy describes organized training pathways in both synchronous and asynchronous formats, open to citizens, businesses, and public administrations and drawing on internal and external specialists. For AI literacy, the inspected pages show webinars and events covering topics such as AI applications, public-sector use, regulation, responsibility, and risks; recordings and written summaries let people revisit material asynchronously. This supports a mix of scheduled instruction and self-paced review, but the pages do not establish a more specific teaching method, such as project-based learning or assessment. AgID’s AI page also lists training meetings and recordings for several audiences. Sources: https://www.agid.gov.it/it/academy and https://www.agid.gov.it/it/ambiti-intervento/intelligenza-artificiale
prioritySummary: AgID’s broad emphasis is advancing Italy’s digital transition: coordinating public administrations, improving public digital services, and spreading digital skills among citizens, businesses, and government. In its AI-related work, the site specifically says AgID supports and trains administrations and businesses in effective and safe AI use, while its Academy and AI events also address public officials, ICT and innovation companies, academia, researchers, and citizens. The inspected evidence therefore points to both institutional capacity-building and wider digital literacy, with public administration particularly prominent, rather than a single exclusive beneficiary or an explicitly ranked set of priorities. Sources: https://www.agid.gov.it/it/agenzia, https://www.agid.gov.it/it/ambiti-intervento/intelligenza-artificiale, and https://www.agid.gov.it/it/academy

The AI section links to recordings and documents on AI history, applications, public-administration use, and related topics, but does not name a dedicated platform or software used to deliver them. metadata.Initiative / Programme: Certificazione "Scuola AI Friendly" (Scuola Etica Digitale)
metadata.Description: School certification scheme referenced by respondent.

summary: Scuola AI Friendly is an Italian school-level certification scheme intended to support the responsible integration of AI in education. It offers schools an initial consultation and guidance toward certification, with advanced training to help teachers guide AI use and prepare students for an AI-shaped world. Linked courses cover AI concepts and classroom uses, data and probabilistic thinking, and ethical concerns including bias, inclusion, privacy, and human oversight. Described learning activities include practical projects, discussions of ethical dilemmas, simulations, and student presentations; no specific instructional platform is identified.
pedagogicalSummary: The initiative describes active, applied learning rather than relying on extended lectures. Student courses feature interactive discussions of ethical dilemmas, collaborative AI projects, digital simulations, and student-led presentations. Teacher and trainer courses add practical exercises with educational datasets, maker and creative activities, project work, and the use of AI prediction as a context for learning probability and responsibility. Simulations and digital twins are presented as ways to explore complex scenarios safely; portfolios and assessment rubrics document learning. SERENDIP-EDU is named as a framework for designing teaching activities. These approaches are described on the course pages, although the school-certification page itself gives little detail about classroom practice. Sources: https://scuolaeticadigitale.it/programmi-_e_corsi_scuola_etica_digitale_ai/ ; https://scuolaeticadigitale.it/corsi-docenti-scuola-etica-ai/ ; https://scuolaeticadigitale.it/corso-formatore-certificato-faies/
prioritySummary: The certification principally aims to help schools integrate AI into their educational work in a conscious, ethical, and responsible way. It explicitly emphasizes advanced teacher training so qualified educators can guide AI use across school settings, while preparing students for an AI-shaped world through ethical AI practices and responsible digital citizenship. The wider initiative also describes critical and responsible AI use, inclusion, privacy, and human oversight as educational concerns. Its intended beneficiaries therefore include teachers and school leaders who need practical guidance, as well as students and the broader school community. The accessible pages present these priorities together rather than establishing a clear hierarchy beyond the certification's focus on schools and teacher preparation. Sources: https://scuolaeticadigitale.it/certificazione-scuola-ai-friendly/ ; https://scuolaeticadigitale.it/chi-siamo/
educationalTechnologySummary: The inspected pages do not name a particular software platform, AI product, or hardware that the initiative develops or uses for instruction. They do describe learning activities involving AI prediction, including mini-exercises using school datasets, and digital simulations and “digital twins” for exploring scenarios safely. These are presented as elements of course methodology, but the pages do not specify which tools implement them or whether they are built by the initiative, so no proprietary educational technology can be identified from this evidence. The initiative also refers generally to classroom tools and resources without naming them. This is a limitation of the pages inspected, not confirmation that no additional technologies are used. Sources: https://scuolaeticadigitale.it/corsi-docenti-scuola-etica-ai/ ; https://scuolaeticadigitale.it/corso-formatore-certificato-faies/
