metadata.Initiative / Programme: IC3 Modena – "Lucy" document
metadata.Description: School resource referenced by respondent.

summary: Lucy is an experimental AI education programme developed at Istituto Comprensivo 3 di Modena in collaboration with Ammagamma. It serves lower-secondary students through seven two-hour sessions delivered during regular school hours, with teachers also identified as intended learners. The interdisciplinary, “learning by doing and thinking” approach connects AI concepts and models with mathematics, logic, philosophy and data literacy. Students explore AI’s capabilities, applications, benefits and risks, practise interpreting data responsibly, and are assessed through work contributing to subject grades.
pedagogicalSummary: The document describes a curriculum-based, interdisciplinary approach combining technical and scientific learning with education about complexity and critical thinking. The programme is organized as seven two-hour sessions for all third-year middle-school classes, during regular school hours, with assessment contributing to technology, mathematics and language grades. Its stated model is “learning by doing and thinking”: students study AI concepts and models, try theory in practice, interpret data and are encouraged to ask questions about AI’s capabilities and applications. The document also highlights sensory experience and links AI with algebra, statistics, logic, problem-solving, philosophy and imagination. These details support an active, inquiry-oriented approach, though specific lesson plans or activities are not provided. (https://www.ic3modena.edu.it/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/Lucy.pdf)
prioritySummary: Lucy principally aims to help young people—and also teachers—understand and use AI and interpret data consciously and responsibly. The document emphasizes middle-school students’ awareness of AI’s mechanisms, capabilities, benefits and possible risks, alongside critical engagement with digital technology and the relationship between real and virtual experience. It also seeks to encourage interest in mathematics and AI and develop new competencies. The initiative frames education as supporting cultural innovation and social inclusion, and mentions sustainable social and productive futures; these are broader aspirations rather than a more precisely specified programme outcome. The inspected document identifies the intended beneficiaries and aims but does not provide evidence about measured impact or implementation beyond the described school programme. (https://www.ic3modena.edu.it/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/Lucy.pdf)
educationalTechnologySummary: The document presents AI and data science as subjects students learn about, including their mechanisms, models, capabilities and applications; it does not identify a particular educational platform, software package, device or hardware used or developed by Lucy. It mentions students interpreting data and trying theory in practice, but gives no details about the tools or materials involved, so these activities should not be taken as evidence of a specific technology. AI itself is the topic of instruction, not a named learning technology used by the initiative. The inspected PDF therefore supports describing the educational focus, but not identifying particular educational technologies; whether any are used is not established by this source. (https://www.ic3modena.edu.it/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/Lucy.pdf)

inclusion.reason: The document explicitly presents an educational initiative on AI literacy for students in secondary schools (middle school level), including curriculum content, learning objectives, teaching methods, and assessment procedures that explain how AI works and how to use it critically. The initiative has backing from a public school (Istituto Comprensivo 3 di Modena), mentions collaboration with UNESCO Italy and EU representation, which qualifies under the intergovernmental or government-endorsed inclusion route. Although originally implemented in one school, its reference to being 'the first AI school in Italy' suggests potential wider relevance, but even without confirmed national-scale adoption, the presence of endorsement from public institutions and international bodies (UNESCO/ EU) supports inclusion under an inclusion route. Uncertainty: no evidence of widespread adoption across multiple schools or regions beyond IC3 Modena is visible on this page alone, but this does not preclude inclusion given the institutional endorsements.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: InnovaMenti (MIM/Équipe Formative Territoriali)
metadata.Description: MIM training pathway, delivered by regional teacher teams, using four DigComp2.2-inspired modules to build teachers' critical AI use.

summary: InnovaMenti_Intelligenza Artificiale is a teacher-development pathway delivered by Italy’s Territorial Training Teams in Basilicata. Its four modules—Comunicare_AI, Vedere_AI, Sentire_AI and Agire_AI—draw on DigComp 2.2 and aim to support conscious, critical use of AI in teaching across humanities and sciences. The wider offer promotes active, collaborative pedagogy and digital citizenship, with classroom lesson plans and activities and opportunities for teachers to share practice. The available descriptions do not specify the modules’ activities or training formats.
pedagogicalSummary: The accessible description presents teacher learning as practical and reflective: educators are encouraged to rethink everyday practice through active methodologies, collaborative planning, flexible learning environments, and considered use of technology. InnovaMenti_Intelligenza Artificiale introduces AI through four modules—Comunicare_AI, Vedere_AI, Sentire_AI, and Agire_AI—described as inspired by DigComp 2.2 and spanning humanities and sciences. The wider offer also includes teaching materials, activity sheets, and lesson plans intended for classroom use, alongside opportunities for teachers to exchange practices in learning communities. The pages do not detail session formats, assessment, or the specific activities within the four AI modules, so the precise teaching methods used in that pathway remain unclear. (https://www.mim.gov.it/web/basilicata/-/le-proposte-delle-equipe-formative-territoriali-tra-didattica-attiva-ia-e-cittadinanza-digitale; https://scuolafutura.pubblica.istruzione.it/eft-basilicata)
prioritySummary: The AI pathway’s stated emphasis is helping teachers develop a conscious and critical use of AI in teaching, with exposure to AI-related tools and concepts across both humanities and scientific subjects. The broader work of the Territorial Training Teams also supports teachers’ digital teaching capabilities and students’ digital skills, while encouraging collaboration among schools and sharing effective practices. The article situates InnovaMenti within a wider digital-citizenship and school-innovation offer, but does not establish a single overarching priority or rank these aims. The inspected pages therefore support a teacher-development emphasis for the AI pathway, alongside wider school-community and student digital-competence goals. (https://www.mim.gov.it/web/basilicata/-/le-proposte-delle-equipe-formative-territoriali-tra-didattica-attiva-ia-e-cittadinanza-digitale; https://scuolafutura.pubblica.istruzione.it/eft-basilicata)
educationalTechnologySummary: The pages identify Scuola Futura as the platform through which the Territorial Training Teams offer learning pathways, and describe a freely accessible resource section containing lesson plans for classroom use. These are digital means of accessing training and teaching materials, but the inspected descriptions do not specify features that make the platform itself an instructional tool beyond hosting the offer and resources. The AI pathway refers generally to becoming familiar with tools and languages associated with AI, but names no particular AI application, software, hardware, or platform for learning. The evidence therefore supports use of Scuola Futura to access training and materials, but does not establish that the initiative develops or uses any specific educational AI technology. (https://www.mim.gov.it/web/basilicata/-/le-proposte-delle-equipe-formative-territoriali-tra-didattica-attiva-ia-e-cittadinanza-digitale; https://scuolafutura.pubblica.istruzione.it/eft-basilicata)

inclusion.reason: The initiative includes AI literacy, specifically focusing on 'critical AI use'. It meets the inclusion criteria because it is issued, funded, or formally endorsed by a sub-national government body (the Basilicata Regional Directorate of Schools/MIM, indicated by 'mim.gov.it' and 'Basilicata'), which qualifies under the government endorsement route.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Liceo Stellini (Udine) – "Costruire il futuro: l'IA entra a scuola"
metadata.Description: School initiative referenced by respondent.

summary: “Costruire il futuro: l’IA entra a scuola” is a school-network initiative coordinated by Liceo Classico Statale Jacopo Stellini in Udine. In 2023/24, 55 schools in Friuli Venezia Giulia collaborated on professional development for school staff and shared guidance on generative AI in education. The initiative provides guidance and related training materials addressing classroom and curricular integration, student involvement, ethics, privacy, and data protection. Its documented approach emphasizes collaboration and resource-sharing among educators; the available evidence does not detail a direct student-instruction programme.
pedagogicalSummary: The initiative’s documented learning approach is primarily professional development for school staff, rather than a described programme of direct instruction for students. In 2023/24, 55 Friuli Venezia Giulia schools collaborated on training and on producing shared guidance for using generative AI in teaching. Learning and coordination were supported through periodic in-person and online meetings that enabled exchange of ideas and updates; a coordination committee facilitated collaboration, and a scientific committee reviewed and validated the final guidance. The guidance addresses classroom integration, student involvement, ethics, privacy, and data protection. This supports a collaborative, resource-sharing approach, but the inspected page does not detail teaching methods or activities used with students. Source: https://stelliniudine.edu.it/costruire-il-futuro-lia-entra-a-scuola/
prioritySummary: The clearest emphasis is strengthening school staff capacity and helping participating institutions make informed use of generative AI for teaching. The network of 55 schools aimed to train personnel and produce accessible, shared guidance; member schools also committed to promoting its adoption and sharing experiences and good practices. The guidance’s stated scope includes ethical use, curricular integration, student engagement, privacy, and data protection, indicating concern for how AI affects teaching and learners as well as staff development. The inspected page does not establish a separate workforce or societal priority, nor does it quantify outcomes; its evidence points chiefly to supporting schools and educators in responsible pedagogical use. Source: https://stelliniudine.edu.it/costruire-il-futuro-lia-entra-a-scuola/
educationalTechnologySummary: The page describes generative AI as the subject of the initiative’s guidance and training, and lists materials and presentations about chatbots and tools such as ChatGPT. These references establish topics of discussion, not that the initiative uses or develops those products as learning technologies. It also names “MIND IN CLASS,” described as an assistant intended to help school leaders and teachers plan educational pathways informed by cognitive-neuroscience evidence, with prompts concerning AI, attention, memory, motivation, brain plasticity, and classroom emotions. The inspected page does not clarify whether this assistant was developed by the initiative, how it is accessed, or whether it was used in the training. No other specific educational platform, software, or hardware is documented as deployed. Source: https://stelliniudine.edu.it/costruire-il-futuro-lia-entra-a-scuola/

inclusion.reason: The initiative includes AI literacy through its dedicated section on the school website providing educational content about artificial intelligence. While it is a single-institution project, as per calibration examples (e.g., university courses with plausible wider audience), it does not need government mandate or large-scale adoption to qualify because it contains explicit AI literacy elements that are educational in nature rather than just using AI tools for education.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Linee guida per le discipline STEM (2023)
metadata.Description: MIM guidelines (Sept 2023) strengthening STEM and digital competences across all school levels.

summary: Italy’s Ministry of Education and Merit issued these 2023 guidelines to help schools strengthen mathematics, science, technology, and digital competences across school levels. Addressed to school leaders, teachers, and students, they encourage schools to include relevant actions in their three-year educational plans and promote innovative teaching approaches. Within this broader STEM guidance, the document discusses conscious use of AI, potential educational benefits and risks, and issues including ethics, rights, and student data protection.
pedagogicalSummary: The guidelines are intended to prompt schools to include actions in their three-year educational plans that strengthen mathematics, science, technology, and digital competences through “innovative teaching methodologies,” according to the MIM announcement (https://www.mim.gov.it/web/guest/-/emanate-le-linee-guida-per-le-discipline-stem). This supports describing the initiative as encouraging pedagogical innovation within school curricula, but the accessible announcement does not identify particular methods or explain how learning activities are organised. Although the guidelines PDF is linked to the initiative (https://www.mim.gov.it/documents/20182/0/linee_guida_stem-stampa.pdf/c9144007-9a2b-3424-acf0-8995165b7ac2?t=1703239847755), its extracted text was too large to inspect in detail here; therefore, more specific approaches cannot be confirmed from this limited review.
prioritySummary: The initiative’s stated emphasis is strengthening mathematical, scientific, technological, and digital competences in schools. The MIM says the guidelines were sent to school leaders, teachers, and students and are meant to introduce related actions into schools’ three-year educational plans (https://www.mim.gov.it/web/guest/-/emanate-le-linee-guida-per-le-discipline-stem). The available evidence therefore points principally to school-based learning and competence development, with school staff and students among the intended beneficiaries. The announcement describes digital competence alongside STEM rather than setting out a distinct AI-literacy objective. The guidelines PDF is the underlying document, but its full contents could not be examined in detail in this inspection (https://www.mim.gov.it/documents/20182/0/linee_guida_stem-stampa.pdf/c9144007-9a2b-3424-acf0-8995165b7ac2?t=1703239847755), so further priorities cannot be established here.
educationalTechnologySummary: The MIM announcement identifies digital competence as one of the areas to be strengthened, alongside mathematics, science, and technology, and says this should be pursued through innovative teaching methodologies (https://www.mim.gov.it/web/guest/-/emanate-le-linee-guida-per-le-discipline-stem). However, the inspected announcement does not name any educational software, platform, device, or other technology that the initiative develops or uses to support learning. Digital competence is a learning goal, not evidence by itself of a particular educational technology. The linked guidelines PDF is the main supporting document, but its extracted text could not be reviewed in detail here (https://www.mim.gov.it/documents/20182/0/linee_guida_stem-stampa.pdf/c9144007-9a2b-3424-acf0-8995165b7ac2?t=1703239847755); consequently, no specific tools can be confirmed from this limited inspection.

inclusion.reason: Government issuance qualifies under the inclusion route ('Issued…by a national or sub-national government') even though AI-literacy content is not clearly present in this text. Government status alone satisfies an inclusion criterion per the screening rules; uncertainty about specific AI literacy elements does not override the government-route inclusion.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Piano Nazionale Scuola Digitale (PNSD)
metadata.Description: National plan for digital innovation in schools.

summary: The Piano Nazionale Scuola Digitale (PNSD) is a multi-year Italian Ministry of Education plan for digital innovation across the school system. It aims to improve students’ competencies and learning while supporting teachers and other school staff in educational and organizational change. The plan promotes technology as a means to support teaching and learning, alongside digital learning environments, computational thinking, digital citizenship, and media education. It is a broad digital-education strategy rather than an AI-focused literacy initiative, though the associated framework includes some material on AI in education.
pedagogicalSummary: The plan frames digital-era education as a cultural and educational change, not simply the introduction of devices. It describes school as an open learning space and calls for technology to serve teaching and learning while preserving intensive teacher–student interaction. Learning is oriented toward students’ competencies, learning outcomes, transversal skills, and capacities useful in a changing world; the plan also situates learning across lifelong and formal and non-formal contexts. It expects teachers to address methodological and teaching challenges and the wider school staff to be supported through change. The inspected pages do not identify a specific classroom method or detailed learning sequence, so approaches such as project-based learning cannot be confirmed. (https://www.mim.gov.it/web/guest/scuola-digitale)
prioritySummary: The PNSD principally seeks broad innovation of Italy’s school system and a repositioning of education for the digital age. Its stated educational aims include improving students’ competencies, learning, and outcomes, and preparing them to contribute as individuals, citizens, and professionals. It also emphasizes enabling and supporting all school personnel—not only teachers—to take part in educational and organizational change, and seeks impact across the country through coordinated investment and collaboration among schools, government bodies, and other partners. The pages present these as connected priorities rather than establishing a single narrower beneficiary or ranking. The inspected material describes a general digital-education plan, not an AI-specific literacy initiative. (https://www.mim.gov.it/web/guest/scuola-digitale; https://www.mim.gov.it/web/guest/innovazione-digitale)
educationalTechnologySummary: The inspected pages do not name a particular educational platform, software product, device, or technology developed by the PNSD. They describe technologies in general as enabling, everyday tools placed in service of school activities, especially teaching and learning, and envisage their use across classrooms, shared areas, laboratories, individual spaces, and informal settings. This is a stated direction for integrating technology into school environments, not evidence that the initiative itself develops or deploys a specific tool. The pages also caution against treating technology deployment as the plan’s purpose in itself. Because the inspection covered the overview and an MIM innovation page rather than the plan’s full implementation materials, specific technologies used by individual schools may not be represented. (https://www.mim.gov.it/web/guest/scuola-digitale; https://www.mim.gov.it/web/guest/innovazione-digitale)

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Strategia Nazionale per le Competenze Digitali & Operational Plan (Repubblica Digitale)
metadata.Description: National digital skills strategy under the Repubblica Digitale initiative.

summary: Repubblica Digitale is Italy’s national digital-skills strategy and operational plan, led by the Department for Digital Transformation. It aims to reduce the digital divide and strengthen digital competencies across education, the workforce, public administration, businesses and the wider public, through four areas: institutional culture, workforce skills, civic culture and monitoring. The initiative sets objectives and tracks progress, while its related resources include multimedia learning, video lessons, a self-assessment test and digital facilitation services. These services describe tailored, incremental learning, including practical exercises, one-to-one support and self-study. AI appears among the topics in the resource catalogue, but the strategy is broader digital-skills development rather than a dedicated AI-literacy programme.
pedagogicalSummary: Repubblica Digitale is a national strategy spanning multiple programmes, so the inspected pages do not establish one pedagogy for all its activities. They do describe the Digital Facilitation Points’ approach: support is tailored to each citizen’s needs and starting skills, with learning sequenced incrementally against the DigComp framework. Activities include personalized one-to-one assistance, online and asynchronous self-study, and small-group micro-courses involving practical exercises and problem-solving. The project explicitly promotes “learning by doing” and a flipped-learning approach: participants can study materials independently, while facilitators use face-to-face time to check understanding and support progress. This is evidence about digital-skills learning generally; the pages do not specify a distinct teaching method for AI literacy. (https://repubblicadigitale.gov.it/portale/progetti-del-dipartimento/rete-dei-servizi-di-facilitazione-digitale; https://repubblicadigitale.gov.it/portale/strategia)
prioritySummary: The initiative principally aims to reduce Italy’s digital divide and build digital skills across the population, with inclusion and citizens’ ability to use digital services and participate in civic life prominent in its stated goals. Its strategy also addresses education and higher education, the active workforce, specialist ICT skills, and citizens; it sets goals concerning basic and advanced skills, ICT graduates, workers, businesses, and use of public digital services. The stated rationale links skills both to people’s opportunities—including employability and exercising citizenship rights—and to Italy’s economic and social development. The inspected pages therefore support a broad, multi-group priority rather than a single workforce-only or AI-specific emphasis. (https://repubblicadigitale.gov.it/portale/programma; https://repubblicadigitale.gov.it/portale/strategia; https://repubblicadigitale.gov.it/portale/progetti-del-dipartimento/rete-dei-servizi-di-facilitazione-digitale)
educationalTechnologySummary: The initiative’s pages identify several learning resources and one operational platform, but do not indicate that Repubblica Digitale developed all of them. Its training offer includes multimedia learning units, and its competence-development pages point citizens to video lessons on YouTube and an online self-assessment test that suggests skills to improve and relevant resources. The catalog includes AI among its searchable topics. The Department-developed Facilita platform is used to manage and monitor digital facilitation and training services and to support facilitator collaboration; the page describes it as an operational and community tool, not a teaching platform for learners. The programme timeline also records the Italian release of Elements of AI, a course created by the University of Helsinki and Reaktor in collaboration with COTEC and Roma Tre; it does not identify it as a Repubblica Digitale-developed technology. (https://repubblicadigitale.gov.it/portale/sviluppa-le-tue-competenze; https://repubblicadigitale.gov.it/servizi/offerta-formativa; https://repubblicadigitale.gov.it/portale/progetti-del-dipartimento/piattaforma-facilita; https://repubblicadigitale.gov.it/portale/programma)

inclusion.reason: The initiative is issued and mandated by the Presidency of the Council of Ministers (Presidenza del Consiglio dei ministri), a national government body of Italy, which satisfies the inclusion route requiring formal government endorsement. The strategic document (Strategia Nazionale per le competenze digitali) and operational plan explicitly focus on digital competence building with learning objectives (e.g., reducing the digital skills gap, increasing ICT specialists, fostering civic digital culture). This fulfills the AI-literacy requirement: the initiative includes educational content and guidance about how to use AI and digital tools. No exclusion criteria apply.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Regione Lombardia – Google for Education agreement for ITS (2026/27)
metadata.Description: Regione Lombardia and Google for Education signed a 2026/27 agreement to train and certify ITS teachers and students in AI via Gemini.

summary: Regione Lombardia and Google for Education have agreed to provide AI training and certification for teachers and students at ITS higher technical institutes in Lombardy, starting in the 2026/27 academic year. Teachers will follow a “Train the Trainer” pathway, while students will take part in the Gemini Academy using Gemini for Education. The initiative emphasizes practical AI skills for professional development alongside legal and ethical awareness and responsible use; the available description does not specify course content or teaching methods in detail.
pedagogicalSummary: The agreement describes two organised learning tracks beginning in academic year 2026/27: a “Train the Trainer” pathway and certification for ITS teachers, followed by Google for Education’s Gemini Academy and student certification. This suggests a trainer-preparation model supporting teacher and student learning, with Google experts providing support, but the article gives no detail on lesson formats, activities, or assessment beyond certification. It also identifies legal and ethical awareness alongside practical AI skills as important learning content. A separate 2025 regional article discusses learning by doing, peer tutoring, and project-based learning as part of a broader proposed renewal of vocational education; it does not establish that these methods are part of this agreement. Sources: https://www.lombardianotizie.online/intelligenza-artificiale-its-lombardia/ and https://www.lombardianotizie.online/ia-scuola-professionali-lombardia/
prioritySummary: The initiative principally aims to build AI competence among teachers and students at Lombardy’s ITS higher technical institutes, with a strong vocational and workforce orientation. The regional and Google representatives frame training and recognised certification as ways to prepare young people for a changing labour market, increase their professional value and meet employers’ demand for advanced skills. Teacher development is also a stated priority, both as a programme track and as support for integrating AI into ITS education. The article additionally stresses responsible use, including legal and ethical awareness, and describes AI as a tool that should complement rather than replace human work. It does not specify a ranking among these aims. Source: https://www.lombardianotizie.online/intelligenza-artificiale-its-lombardia/
educationalTechnologySummary: The article identifies Gemini for Education as the AI technology used in the planned ITS training initiative. metadata.Initiative / Programme: DigCompLAC – Latin American digital competence framework
metadata.Description: CEPAL/GIZ-backed regional digital competence framework adapted from EU DigComp 2.2 for Latin America and the Caribbean.

summary: DigCompALC is a regional digital-competence framework published by the UN Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean, with support from GIZ, and adapted from the European DigComp 2.2 framework for Latin America and the Caribbean. Developed through co-design informed by regional and national initiatives and stakeholder contributions, it provides a shared language for describing digital competencies and recommendations for implementation. It is intended to guide policymakers, education systems, employers, and social organizations in developing inclusive digital strategies; the available evidence presents it as a reference framework, not a course or teaching programme. Its digital competencies are described as a foundation for digital and AI literacy.
pedagogicalSummary: The inspected CEPAL page describes DigCompALC as a regional digital-competence framework, not as a course or teaching programme. It was developed through a co-design methodology informed by analysis of national and regional digital-skills training initiatives and contributions from policymakers, experts, and technical-community representatives. Co-design describes how the framework was developed; the page does not establish a classroom pedagogy or specify learning activities, assessment, or instructional support. It says the framework is intended to guide education systems and others in designing inclusion-oriented strategies, but the inspected material does not show how those strategies teach. This is a limit of the accessible page, not evidence that no pedagogical approaches are described in the full document. (https://www.cepal.org/es/publicaciones/90120-marco-regional-competencias-digitales-america-latina-caribe-digcompalc)
prioritySummary: The initiative’s stated emphasis is promoting inclusive digital transformation in Latin America and the Caribbean by providing a shared regional language for defining and describing digital competencies in ways responsive to the region’s needs. Its intended beneficiaries and users include the region’s population, as well as policymakers, education systems, employers, and social organizations that may use the framework to design inclusion-oriented strategies. The page situates the publication in productive and enterprise development and lists digital government, public policy, innovation, inequality, and industrial development among its topics, but does not establish a specific ranking among these priorities. (https://www.cepal.org/es/publicaciones/90120-marco-regional-competencias-digitales-america-latina-caribe-digcompalc)
educationalTechnologySummary: The inspected page identifies DigCompALC as a digital-competence framework based on and adapted from the European DigComp 2.2 framework. It presents a shared reference for describing competencies and guiding strategies, rather than naming a software platform, learning-management system, application, or hardware used to teach them. The page does not identify educational technologies developed or deployed by the initiative; the framework itself is a reference document, not evidence of a technology used for learning. This finding is limited to the publication page inspected, so additional details about implementation or tools may appear in the full document or elsewhere. (https://www.cepal.org/es/publicaciones/90120-marco-regional-competencias-digitales-america-latina-caribe-digcompalc)

inclusion.reason: The initiative qualifies for inclusion because it is issued by CEPAL (ECLAC), which is a UN subregional body (intergovernmental organization). It includes substantive AI-literacy-aligned content through its definition of digital competencies that serve as the foundation for digital and AI literacy, providing guidance to policy makers and education systems. The framework has a regional scope with evidence of relevance across multiple jurisdictions in Latin America and the Caribbean, satisfying the inclusion route for an intergovernmental body or a framework used by several jurisdictions.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Guidelines for ethical use of AI in science and study process (Academic Ethics Ombudsperson)
metadata.Description: Guidelines approved by Lithuania's Office of the Academic Ethics and Procedures Controller (April 2024) on ethical AI use in academia.

summary: Approved in April 2024 by Lithuania’s Office of the Academic Ethics and Procedures Controller, these guidelines address ethical AI use in research and higher education. They provide principles for academic communities and advice to institutions developing AI-use policies, covering topics such as intellectual property, user protection, open science, publication ethics, and the evaluation and validation of AI tools. The initiative is policy guidance rather than a teaching programme, and the available evidence does not specify AI-literacy learning activities or delivery technologies.
pedagogicalSummary: The inspected AI-guidelines announcement describes a policy and guidance document, not a teaching program: it outlines ethical principles and advises institutions on preparing AI-use policies, but does not specify a learning sequence, classroom method, or AI-literacy teaching activities (https://etikostarnyba.lt/patvirtintos-dirbtinio-intelekto-etisko-naudojimo-mokslo-ir-studiju-procese-gaires/). Separately, the Office says its broader academic-ethics trainings aim to strengthen practical competencies, prevent misconduct, and help communities apply principles in practice; institutions can tailor topics and content to their needs (https://etikostarnyba.lt/suaugusiuju-svietimas/). That is evidence of a practical, needs-responsive training approach in the Office’s wider work, but the inspected pages do not establish that these trainings teach AI literacy or describe a specific pedagogy for the AI guidelines.
prioritySummary: The initiative’s stated emphasis is ethical use of AI in science and study, for the benefit of Lithuania’s research and higher-education communities and the institutions that govern their work. The guidelines address general ethical principles, intellectual-property rights, user protection, open science and publication ethics, and evaluation and validation of AI tools. They also aim to help institutions prepare and implement AI-use policies and integrate ethical considerations into rules for research and studies (https://etikostarnyba.lt/patvirtintos-dirbtinio-intelekto-etisko-naudojimo-mokslo-ir-studiju-procese-gaires/). The inspected evidence presents this as an academic integrity and responsible-use emphasis; it does not identify workforce upskilling or individual well-being as the initiative’s principal goal.
educationalTechnologySummary: The inspected pages do not identify a learning platform, software, hardware, or other educational technology developed or used by the Office to teach AI literacy. The AI-guidelines announcement refers to AI tools as subjects for evaluation and validation, and discusses ethical use in research and study, but does not name tools or describe using them to support learning (https://etikostarnyba.lt/patvirtintos-dirbtinio-intelekto-etisko-naudojimo-mokslo-ir-studiju-procese-gaires/). The Office’s adult-education page describes practical trainings for academic communities, but the accessible text does not specify digital delivery tools or AI-specific learning technologies (https://etikostarnyba.lt/suaugusiuju-svietimas/). Thus, no educational technology can be confirmed from the limited pages inspected; this is a limit of available evidence, not proof that none is used.

inclusion.reason: The initiative meets the inclusion criteria via the government route, as it was issued by a statutory body, the Academic Ethics and Procedures Controller (Valstybinė akademinės etikos ir procedūrų kontrolieriaus tarnyba), which is part of the Lithuanian state administration. Although the guidelines focus primarily on ethics rather than technical literacy, they establish the regulatory framework for AI use in academia, serving as a foundational document for AI literacy initiatives in the country.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: KI-Kompass (Luxembourg Ministry of Education)
metadata.Description: Ministry of Education framework and platform with validated AI tools, teacher training and guidance for schools.

summary: KI-Kompass is a Luxembourg Ministry of Education framework and platform supporting AI literacy and responsible AI use in schools. It serves teachers and school leaders through pedagogical guidance, practical classroom materials, training, communities of practice, a glossary and a directory of AI tools; pupils are also addressed through age-appropriate learning resources and classroom activities. Its approach connects learning without AI, about AI and with AI, emphasizing critical thinking, human judgement and responsible use. The platform also presents school projects and pilots, alongside curated third-party tools rather than tools it develops itself.
pedagogicalSummary: The strategy describes an age-appropriate progression linking learning without AI, learning about AI and learning with AI, with space for experimentation and reflection while preserving critical thinking and human judgement. Learning is supported through teacher training, ready-to-use classroom materials and facilitated Communities of Practice: teachers and school leaders test approaches in their own classes, reflect on experience and exchange it with peers, with expert moderation. Training ranges from short hybrid courses to conferences and pedagogical days. These examples indicate a combination of guided professional learning, classroom application and collaborative reflection; the inspected pages do not establish one single teaching method across the initiative. Sources: https://ki-kompass.lu/en/strategie-richtlinien/?modal=modal-block-strategy ; https://ki-kompass.lu/en/weiterbildung-austausch/?modal=modal-block-trainings ; https://ki-kompass.lu/en/weiterbildung-austausch/?modal=modal-block-communities-of-practice
prioritySummary: KI Kompass principally aims to guide and support responsible, transparent and pedagogically meaningful AI use across Luxembourg schools. Its audience includes teachers, school leaders and other education stakeholders; pupils benefit through age-appropriate learning and classroom use. The strategy emphasizes strengthening educators’ understanding and capacity to integrate AI responsibly in teaching and administration, while treating AI as support for learning rather than a replacement for human abilities. It also explicitly prioritizes critical thinking, human judgement and personal responsibility, including the ability to think both with and without AI. The pages present these priorities together rather than establishing a hierarchy among them. Sources: https://ki-kompass.lu/en/strategie-richtlinien/?modal=modal-block-strategy ; https://ki-kompass.lu/en/weiterbildung-austausch/?modal=modal-block-trainings
educationalTechnologySummary: The KI Kompass site functions as a directory of AI tools and classroom resources; the inspected pages do not indicate that KI Kompass itself develops the listed learning platforms. Its tools section describes fobizz, a browser-based platform with AI chat, image generation, worksheet support, whiteboards, polls, recording features and teacher training; Teachino supports lesson preparation, differentiated materials, classroom presentations, interactive AI-chatbot tasks and learner feedback; and Vittascience supports AI, robotics and programming activities through block-based and text-based coding, for individual or collaborative learning. These are presented as platforms teachers and pupils can use, not as KI Kompass products. Sources: https://ki-kompass.lu/en/tools/ ; https://ki-kompass.lu/en/tool/fobizz/ ; https://ki-kompass.lu/en/tool/teachino/ ; https://ki-kompass.lu/en/tool/vittascience/

inclusion.reason: The initiative explicitly provides AI literacy through 'pedagogical ideas,' 'practical guides,' 'glossary,' and resources explaining how to use AI tools responsibly and creatively. The metadata and page confirm it is a framework issued by the Luxembourg Ministry of Education (a national government body), which satisfies the government inclusion route. Adoption is supported by a dedicated platform for schools, training programs, and communities of practice.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Luxembourg AI Academy
metadata.Description: Academy launched June 2026 under the Digital Learning Hub training participants in Python, statistics, machine learning and data science.

summary: The Data & AI Academy is a professional training programme within Luxembourg’s government-backed Digital Learning Hub, serving professionals, jobseekers and career-changers. It develops practical skills in Python, statistics, data science and machine learning through a shared foundation followed by a Data Science or Machine Learning specialisation and a capstone project. Flexible full-time and part-time tracks combine independent online work, collaborative activities and on-site sessions, with an emphasis on preparing participants for technical roles and supporting Luxembourg’s digital workforce.
pedagogicalSummary: The AI Academy describes a structured, practice-led approach rather than traditional lecture-centred teaching. Participants build on prior Python, mathematics and statistics, then develop foundations, specialise in Data Science or Machine Learning, and bring learning together in a capstone project. Learning combines independent online project work with scheduled collaborative activities and regular on-site sessions. The programme highlights hands-on projects, peer-to-peer learning, problem-solving with other participants, and guidance and feedback from industry experts or mentors; the capstone can address a real-world challenge and may involve an industry partner. Flexible intensive and part-time tracks adapt the pace. These approaches are described on the [AI Academy page](https://www.dlh.lu/ai-academy-1) and the [Academy overview](https://www.dlh.lu/academy-1).
prioritySummary: The initiative principally aims to develop advanced digital and AI skills for professional and economic needs. Its stated focus includes preparing specialists for Data Science and Machine Learning roles, helping professionals deepen skills or change careers, and supporting job seekers and people pursuing a first professional opportunity. The wider Digital Learning Hub mission also includes reducing the digital-skills gap and meeting demand for skilled IT professionals. The ministry announcement additionally links the academies to Luxembourg’s digital transformation, technological sovereignty and economic competitiveness. The evidence therefore indicates both individual career development and national workforce and economic objectives, without establishing a single exclusive beneficiary or ranking these aims. Sources: [ministry announcement](https://men.public.lu/fr/actualites/communiques-conference-presse/2026/06/16-academies-digital-learning-hub.html), [AI Academy page](https://www.dlh.lu/ai-academy-1), and [DLH homepage](https://www.dlh.lu/).
educationalTechnologySummary: The inspected pages describe online project work and online preparatory resources and quizzes, alongside on-site learning, but do not identify a named learning platform, software environment or AI tool developed by the initiative. The AI curriculum lists Python, command-line tools, version control and development environments, and established libraries and frameworks as technical learning content; it does not specify which products are used for instruction. Applicants use an Academy admission platform for resources and quizzes, but the platform is not named. Computers are provided for the on-site admission test, not identified as a learning technology. Thus, online resources and the admission platform are the only specifically described digital supports, and evidence about the technologies used during instruction is limited. Sources: [AI Academy page](https://www.dlh.lu/ai-academy-1) and [Academy overview](https://www.dlh.lu/academy-1).

inclusion.reason: The initiative clearly includes AI literacy as it covers machine learning, data science, Python, and statistics (Page: https://men.public.lu/fr/actualites/communiques-conference-presse/2026/06/16-academies-digital-learning-hub.html). It qualifies for inclusion under the government route because it is launched and funded by Luxembourg's Ministry of Education, Children, and Youth. Uncertainty remains regarding the scale of adoption or whether it targets specific educational contexts, but as a national initiative with government backing, it meets the criteria.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Malaysia Digital Education Policy (Dasar Pendidikan Digital) & DELIMa
metadata.Description: Ministry of Education digital education policy implemented via DELIMa platform.

summary: Malaysia’s Ministry of Education oversees the Malaysia Digital Education Policy and DELIMa, a digital learning platform for pupils, teachers and other education users. DELIMa provides access to learning applications and materials, digital training and courses, and tools to support teachers’ lesson planning. The initiative is framed around digital education at the national level, but the available evidence does not establish specific teaching methods or an emphasis on AI literacy.
pedagogicalSummary: The inspected Ministry homepage and DELIMa landing pages do not describe teaching methods, learning activities, or how instruction is organised. DELIMa’s accessible pages show navigation to a sign-in and a parents’ page, but provide no usable detail about pedagogy. The Digital Education Policy itself was not located in the inspected pages, so the lack of pedagogical evidence should not be read as confirmation that the initiative has no teaching approach. This summary is limited to the information visible at https://www.moe.gov.my/ and https://delima.moe-dl.edu.my/.
prioritySummary: The accessible evidence supports only a limited account of the initiative’s emphasis: the Ministry portal links to DELIMa, while DELIMa presents sign-in access and a page for parents, suggesting a digital education service connected with the education community. The inspected pages do not explain the Digital Education Policy’s aims, intended beneficiaries, or whether its principal emphasis is skills, workforce preparation, or wider societal outcomes. The policy page itself was not found, so no priority or hierarchy among possible goals can be established from this inspection. Sources: https://www.moe.gov.my/ and https://delima.moe-dl.edu.my/.
educationalTechnologySummary: DELIMa is the educational platform identified in the inspected material: it is linked from the Ministry portal, and its landing page provides a sign-in link that redirects toward d3.delima.edu.my, alongside a page labelled for parents. These pages establish a platform and access route, but do not reveal its learning tools, content, software integrations, or how teachers and students use it. The Digital Education Policy page and further platform details were not accessible in this limited inspection, so it is not possible to say which specific educational technologies DELIMa develops or uses beyond the platform itself. Sources: https://www.moe.gov.my/ and https://delima.moe-dl.edu.my/.

inclusion.reason: The initiative qualifies for inclusion under the first inclusion route: it is issued by a national government ministry (the Ministry of Education of Malaysia). The DELIMa platform, launched as part of the Malaysia Digital Economy Blueprint and Digital Education Policy, represents a nationwide implementation of digital education with evidence of system-scale adoption. Additionally, the site links to DELIMa and other sub-portals, suggesting the presence of AI literacy components such as lesson plans, tutorials on using AI tools in education, or guidance on responsible AI usage—consistent with typical government-backed digital learning frameworks.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: "AI Made in Morocco" roadmap
metadata.Description: Roadmap unveiled January 2026 by the Ministry of Digital Transition and Administrative Reform, targeting 100bn MAD in AI value, 50,000 jobs and 200,000 people trained in AI skills by 2030.

summary: Maroc IA 2030 is a national AI roadmap launched by Morocco’s Ministry of Digital Transition and Administrative Reform, focused on digital sovereignty, skills development, innovation, and wider AI adoption. It aims by 2030 to generate 100 billion MAD in AI-related value, create 50,000 jobs, and train 200,000 people in AI skills. Its planned Jazari Institutes are intended to support training, applied research, and experimentation, bringing together universities, researchers, startups, project leaders, and businesses, including SMEs. Workshops, seminars, and co-design activities are mentioned, but specific curricula and teaching methods are not described.
pedagogicalSummary: The article describes the Jazari Institutes as hubs for training, applied research, experimentation, and incubation, bringing together universities, researchers, startups, and project leaders. It also mentions workshops, scientific seminars, technical and scientific exchanges, and co-design sessions for the Mistral AI–MTNRA research laboratory. These activities suggest learning and knowledge-sharing alongside research, but the article does not specify curricula, teaching methods, learner assessment, or how training is delivered. The co-design and workshop activities are described in the context of R&D, not as a defined instructional model. Further detail on pedagogy is therefore unavailable in the inspected account. (https://www.moroccoworldnews.com/2026/01/274765/morocco-launches-maroc-ia-2030-roadmap-to-strengthen-ai-governance-digital-sovereignty/)
prioritySummary: Maroc IA 2030 is presented as a national framework for sovereign AI development, with emphasis on digital sovereignty, developing national skills, encouraging innovation, and territorial inclusion. The Jazari Institutes are intended to support training and research, technology-company growth, and AI adoption by small and medium-sized enterprises; regional specialization is to reflect local economic and academic strengths. The roadmap also aims to coordinate public institutions and strengthen Morocco’s regional and African standing in AI. The article identifies these as related priorities but does not establish a hierarchy among them or detail specific beneficiary groups beyond the institutions, businesses, researchers, and skills-development efforts it names. metadata.Initiative / Programme: SLO new core objectives (kerndoelen) for digital literacy
metadata.Description: SLO's 2025 definitive draft core objectives establish digital literacy as a formal curriculum area for Dutch primary and secondary schools for the first time.

summary: SLO’s 2025 definitive draft sets out Dutch core objectives for digital literacy in primary, secondary and special education, giving schools a shared basis for developing their curricula. The objectives cover practical digital skills, critical use of digital media and data, online safety, and the effects of technology on people and society, including examples involving AI. Supporting materials offer explanations, examples and implementation guidance, while allowing schools to adapt teaching to their learners and context; the initiative defines curriculum goals rather than a prescribed teaching method or learner-facing technology.
pedagogicalSummary: This initiative primarily sets curriculum goals rather than delivering lessons, so the inspected pages do not establish a single classroom teaching method. They describe goals spanning what schools provide, what learners should master, and what experiences learners should have; some goals combine mastery and experience. The accompanying guidance says schools can adapt teaching choices to their learners and context, use examples to interpret the goals, and connect digital literacy with other learning areas. One described example is discussing rules for AI development; others include critically examining digital sources and working with data. Learning progressions are being developed with education professionals to help schools translate goals into curricula. These are curriculum and implementation approaches, not evidence of a prescribed pedagogy. Sources: https://www.actualisatiekerndoelen.nl/digitalegeletterdheid/updates/hoe-is-een-kerndoel-opgebouwd ; https://www.actualisatiekerndoelen.nl/digitalegeletterdheid/updates/kerndoelen-digitale-geletterdheid-wat-verandert-er ; https://www.actualisatiekerndoelen.nl/aan-de-slag/leerlijnen
prioritySummary: The initiative’s central priority is establishing digital literacy as a sustained part of the curriculum, giving schools a shared framework for preparing learners to participate in a society shaped by digital technology. It aims for learners to become digitally capable, critical and creative citizens, able to act safely and consciously online and understand technology’s possibilities, limits and effects on people and society. The initiative also emphasizes a common educational foundation across primary, lower-secondary and special education, including attention to learners with specific educational needs. Its stated purpose includes preparation for further education, social participation and personal development, rather than a narrowly workforce-focused agenda. The inspected material describes goals and intended benefits; it does not report measured learner outcomes. Sources: https://www.actualisatiekerndoelen.nl/digitalegeletterdheid/updates/kerndoelen-digitale-geletterdheid-wat-verandert-er ; https://www.actualisatiekerndoelen.nl/digitalegeletterdheid/proces/actualisatie-kerndoelen ; https://www.actualisatiekerndoelen.nl/digitalegeletterdheid/updates/uitgangspunten-nieuwe-kerndoelen
educationalTechnologySummary: The inspected pages identify no dedicated learning platform, instructional software, or hardware developed or adopted by this initiative for teaching digital literacy. The initiative develops curriculum materials instead: goal documents, illustrative examples and, over time, learning progressions intended to help schools design their own curricula. The website also presents knowledge clips and links to webinars and podcasts; these are informational media for explaining the goals and supporting school implementation, not evidence of a learner-facing digital-literacy tool. Although the curriculum discusses computers, software, digital platforms and AI as subject matter, that does not establish that the initiative uses those technologies as educational tools. This summary is limited to the pages inspected; it cannot confirm whether other, unexamined materials include additional technologies. Sources: https://www.actualisatiekerndoelen.nl/digitalegeletterdheid ; https://www.actualisatiekerndoelen.nl/aan-de-slag/kerndoelen ; https://www.actualisatiekerndoelen.nl/aan-de-slag/leerlijnen

inclusion.reason: The initiative meets AI-literacy requirements because it formally establishes digital literacy as a core curriculum area for Dutch primary and secondary schools. SLO is a Dutch organization that works in close collaboration with the government to develop official educational standards; this draft represents formal national-level curriculum guidance meeting the inclusion route of formal endorsement by a statutory body or government-related entity.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: AI-GO! – Framework for AI literacy in education (Npuls)
metadata.Description: Npuls framework "Een raamwerk voor AI-geletterdheid in het onderwijs".

summary: AI-GO! is an evidence-informed framework and practical implementation guide for developing AI literacy in Dutch mbo, hbo and wo education. It supports students and education professionals, as well as institutional staff, in understanding AI literacy and embedding it in curriculum, professional learning and organisational practice. Its eight-step, practice-oriented approach encourages teams to experiment, reflect and improve, with attention to knowledge, skills, ethical awareness, learning activities and assessment. The materials offer guidance rather than a prescribed teaching method or dedicated learning technology.
pedagogicalSummary: AI-GO presents an evidence-informed framework and a practical handreiking rather than a single prescribed teaching method. The framework draws on a review of research and practice examples, with feedback from education professionals through World Cafés. Its implementation guide sets out eight steps for institutions, including designing learning activities and assessment and strengthening knowledge, skills, attitudes and ethical awareness. It describes a cyclical, practice-oriented process: teams can start small, experiment, reflect and scale approaches that work, while embedding AI literacy in curriculum, staff development and ongoing quality improvement. This supports both learners and professionals, but the inspected pages do not specify a particular classroom format or detailed lesson sequence (https://npuls.nl/kennisbank/ai-go-een-raamwerk-voor-ai-geletterdheid-in-het-onderwijs; https://npuls.nl/kennisbank/ai-go-in-actie).
prioritySummary: AI-GO’s main emphasis is helping mbo, hbo and wo institutions develop AI literacy among both learners and education professionals, and make that development a sustained part of teaching and institutional practice. The framework addresses what AI literacy means, why it matters and how professionals can foster it; the accompanying guide supports work across curriculum, professional development and organisational planning. Npuls situates this work within responsible, valuable use of AI and data in education, with attention to knowledge and skills and to safe, reliable and accessible education. The inspected pages describe these aims but do not establish a single beneficiary group or a priority ranking among them (https://npuls.nl/kennisbank/ai-go-een-raamwerk-voor-ai-geletterdheid-in-het-onderwijs; https://npuls.nl/kennisbank/ai-go-in-actie; https://npuls.nl/beloften/ai-waardenvol-inzetten).
educationalTechnologySummary: The inspected AI-GO pages identify a framework and implementation guide available as PDF downloads; these are guidance resources, not software or hardware, and no dedicated digital learning technology for teaching AI literacy is identified there (https://npuls.nl/kennisbank/ai-go-een-raamwerk-voor-ai-geletterdheid-in-het-onderwijs; https://npuls.nl/kennisbank/ai-go-in-actie). Elsewhere, Npuls describes eduGenAI as a platform it is building with partners for safe, responsible use of generative AI in further education. It allows institutions to use different commercial or open-source language models in one environment, but the inspected description does not say that it is specifically a tool for learning AI literacy. The available evidence therefore supports noting eduGenAI as a related educational AI platform, not as a confirmed AI-literacy teaching technology (https://npuls.nl/beloften/ai-waardenvol-inzetten).

inclusion.reason: The framework provides explicit AI-literacy content and guidance. Npuls states that it is funded by the National Growth Fund and involves all 102 public mbo schools, universities of applied sciences, and universities, supporting the government-funding inclusion route. Sources: https://npuls.nl/kennisbank/ai-go-een-raamwerk-voor-ai-geletterdheid-in-het-onderwijs and https://npuls.nl/het-verhaal-van-npuls.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: "Working with AI in primary education" (social partners, 2026)
metadata.Description: A March 2026 guidance document by PO-Raad, AOb, CNV, AVS and FvOv on responsible use of AI by staff in primary schools.

summary: A 2026 guidance document from PO-Raad, AOb, CNV, AVS and FvOv helps Dutch primary schools develop a shared approach to AI literacy and staff professional development. Aimed at school boards, leaders, HR advisers, teachers and other education professionals, it offers a five-step route map for discussion, identifying competencies, developing policy and evaluating practice. It emphasizes responsible, pedagogically informed AI use, including critical assessment and attention to privacy and data; it also addresses helping pupils understand and use AI critically. The resource supports school-level reflection and planning rather than providing a formal course or specific AI technology.
pedagogicalSummary: The initiative supports learning mainly through school-level professional reflection and planning, rather than describing a formal course or classroom teaching method. Its handreiking includes a five-step route map intended to help school teams start a conversation, explore which AI competencies are needed, and develop a shared approach to AI literacy and staff professional development. The guidance also identifies professional competencies such as critically assessing AI and guiding pupils in understanding and critically using it. This is evidence of collaborative, discussion-based and practice-oriented support, but the inspected material does not establish specific training formats, activities, or assessment methods. The PDF was too large to inspect fully, so this account relies chiefly on its accompanying article: https://arbeidsmarktplatformpo.nl/nieuws/nieuwe-handreiking-helpt-scholen-werken-aan-ai-professionalisering-in-het-primair-onderwijs/ and the handreiking cover: https://arbeidsmarktplatformpo.nl/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Handreiking-Werken-met-AI-in-het-primair-onderwijs-Arbeidsmarktplatform-PO.pdf.
prioritySummary: The clearest emphasis is building AI literacy and supporting professional development among staff and school organisations in Dutch primary education. The handreiking is aimed at school boards, school leaders, HR advisers, teachers and other education professionals, and is intended to help them determine relevant competencies and organise development together. It stresses responsible, considered use of AI, including critical evaluation, pedagogical judgement, and care around privacy, data and ethical issues. It also includes helping pupils understand and critically use AI, but the inspected description presents staff and organisational capacity-building as the direct focus. The material does not establish a separate priority such as workforce productivity or individual well-being. Evidence: https://arbeidsmarktplatformpo.nl/nieuws/nieuwe-handreiking-helpt-scholen-werken-aan-ai-professionalisering-in-het-primair-onderwijs/; https://arbeidsmarktplatformpo.nl/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Handreiking-Werken-met-AI-in-het-primair-onderwijs-Arbeidsmarktplatform-PO.pdf. The PDF could not be fully inspected.
educationalTechnologySummary: The accessible description identifies no named learning platform, software, hardware, or AI literacy technology developed or deployed by the initiative. Its stated resource is a guidance document: a handreiking with relevant competency examples and a five-step route map for schools to discuss and develop AI literacy and professionalisation. The article mentions AI applications in general—such as lesson preparation, creating teaching materials and supporting differentiation—but as examples of AI’s possible role in education, not as technologies the initiative uses to deliver learning. The evidence therefore supports describing the handreiking as a practical informational resource, not claiming use of a particular educational technology. This conclusion is limited because the PDF was too large to inspect fully. Sources: https://arbeidsmarktplatformpo.nl/nieuws/nieuwe-handreiking-helpt-scholen-werken-aan-ai-professionalisering-in-het-primair-onderwijs/ and https://arbeidsmarktplatformpo.nl/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Handreiking-Werken-met-AI-in-het-primair-onderwijs-Arbeidsmarktplatform-PO.pdf.

inclusion.reason: The document is a formal guidance publication issued by social partners representing primary education stakeholders in the Netherlands, meeting the inclusion route of being endorsed by professional bodies associated with national/sectoral governance. The content clearly includes AI literacy components: it outlines ethical considerations (privacy, data use, accuracy), pedagogical implications, and provides concrete steps for educators to understand and responsibly adopt AI in teaching and administration. While published as a guidance tool, it serves educational staff rather than being merely an AI product.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: AI assessment framework for primary & secondary education (SIVON/Kennisnet, 2026)
metadata.Description: SIVON, with Kennisnet, published an assessment framework (April 2026) helping schools check AI systems against EU AI Act requirements.

summary: SIVON and Kennisnet jointly published a Dutch-language AI assessment framework for primary and secondary education in April 2026. Aimed at helping schools assess AI systems, it provides step-by-step guidance on whether the EU AI Act applies and which risk classification is relevant, alongside measures and FAQs. It is a practical compliance and risk-assessment resource rather than a teaching programme for learners.
pedagogicalSummary: The inspected page presents an assessment framework, not a teaching programme: it asks users to assess step by step whether an AI system falls under the EU AI Act and what risk classification applies. Its sections include an introduction, step-by-step guidance, measures and FAQs, but the accessible evidence does not describe lessons, learner activities or a teaching method for developing AI literacy. This is missing evidence about pedagogy in the inspected material, rather than proof that SIVON or Kennisnet offer no such activities elsewhere. (https://www.sivon.nl/toetsingskader/)
prioritySummary: The initiative’s stated emphasis is helping the foundational-education sector assess AI systems against the EU AI Act, including whether the Act applies and which risk classification is relevant. The page identifies the intended context as foundational education and describes a step-by-step assessment; this supports a priority of enabling informed assessment of AI use in schools, rather than a stated goal of directly teaching AI literacy or workforce upskilling. The inspected page does not clarify which roles within schools are the principal users or set out a broader hierarchy of benefits. (https://www.sivon.nl/toetsingskader/)
educationalTechnologySummary: The page identifies an AI assessment framework and offers a PDF download, alongside a web page with sections for the introduction, step-by-step guidance, measures and FAQs. These are presented as ways to consult the framework for assessing AI systems and their EU AI Act risk classification, not as technologies for teaching learners about AI. No learning platform, educational software or hardware is identified as developed or used to support AI-literacy instruction in the inspected material. Because the page’s accessible description is focused on assessment and regulation, this is a limit of the evidence, not confirmation that the initiative uses no other learning technologies. (https://www.sivon.nl/toetsingskader/)

inclusion.reason: The initiative qualifies under the government/statutory body inclusion route: it is published by SIVON (statutory body of the Dutch Ministry of Education) and Kennisnet (national ICT platform for education funded by the Dutch government). It includes educational guidance content about assessing AI systems, which constitutes AI literacy about how to work with AI tools and their requirements. URL: https://www.sivon.nl/toetsingskader/

metadata.Initiative / Programme: AI Deltaplan
metadata.Description: A late-2025 expert-authored national AI strategy proposal for the Netherlands with 52 recommendations, including AI literacy in education.

summary: AI Deltaplan is a late-2025, expert-authored proposal for Dutch national AI strategy, commissioned by the Ministry of Economic Affairs and setting out 52 recommendations. It addresses national AI knowledge, talent and infrastructure, responsible development and adoption by businesses and government, and societal impacts. Its education-related proposals include practical AI training and a national effort to build AI literacy, but the available evidence describes these as recommendations rather than an implemented teaching programme or specified pedagogy.
pedagogicalSummary: The inspected pages present AI Plan primarily as a policy initiative, not a provider of teaching activities, so they do not establish an implemented pedagogy. Its original proposal recommends a national campaign to make the Netherlands AI-literate, attentive to both opportunities and risks, alongside practical training to encourage AI use in businesses (https://aiplan.nl/ons-voorstel). An open letter calls for investment in AI literacy for all Dutch people (https://aiplan.nl/openbrief). These are proposed goals and training directions, not evidence of a particular teaching method, curriculum, or learning format. The inspected material therefore supports a distinction between an aspiration to develop broad AI skills and a pedagogy actually used by the initiative; the latter could not be identified.
prioritySummary: AI Plan’s central emphasis is to prepare the Netherlands for the AI transition and strengthen its ability to develop, adopt, and govern AI responsibly. Its national plan, commissioned by the Ministry of Economic Affairs, highlights investment in Dutch AI knowledge, talent and infrastructure, faster adoption by businesses and government, and attention to societal impact (https://aiplan.nl/). The original proposal also calls for practical AI training and a national campaign to make people AI-literate (https://aiplan.nl/ons-voorstel), while an open letter specifies AI literacy for all Dutch people and links it to democratic control and reduced dependence on foreign systems (https://aiplan.nl/openbrief). The pages thus indicate connected economic, national-capacity and societal priorities, without establishing AI literacy as the initiative’s sole or primary activity.
educationalTechnologySummary: The inspected pages do not identify an educational technology, learning platform, software product, or hardware developed or used by AI Plan to teach AI literacy. The initiative’s original proposal recommends practical training and a national campaign to build AI skills, but does not specify the tools or learning technologies those activities would use (https://aiplan.nl/ons-voorstel). The open letter likewise calls for AI-literacy investment without naming educational technologies (https://aiplan.nl/openbrief). AI systems and infrastructure discussed on the site are framed as subjects of national policy, development, or adoption—not as educational technologies used by AI Plan for learning. This is a finding about the inspected pages; it does not establish that no such tools exist elsewhere.

inclusion.reason: AI-literacy requirement met: the initiative includes education-related recommendations specifically addressing AI literacy. Inclusion route met: it is a formal national-level strategy document issued under the auspices of Dutch government policy (the Deltaplan process) and intended for adoption by the Dutch government, qualifying as nationally endorsed/funded government work. The page links to PDFs and detailed chapters confirming education focus.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Kennisnet six-step AI policy plan for school boards
metadata.Description: Kennisnet guidance on AI in education.

summary: Kennisnet provides Dutch primary and secondary schools with a six-step guide for developing AI policy aligned with their educational vision and values. Aimed at school boards and the wider school community, it encourages consultation with staff, students and parents while considering AI’s opportunities, risks, permitted uses, safety and privacy. The guide includes an adaptable policy document, and related AI-literacy resources help schools assess staff development needs and plan professional learning; no prescribed classroom pedagogy or dedicated AI platform is established by the available evidence.
pedagogicalSummary: The six-step plan is policy guidance, not a teaching programme, so the inspected pages do not establish a classroom pedagogy. It does recommend a participatory, discussion-based process: schools consult teachers, students, parents and the participation council, consider AI’s opportunities and risks, and develop shared policy linked to school values. For staff AI literacy, related guidance suggests assessing team needs and using a team session to identify professional-development needs; it also notes that training can be organised in different ways, including internally or with external experts. These are approaches to organisational learning and staff development, not evidence of a prescribed instructional method. Evidence: https://www.kennisnet.nl/stappenplan/ai-beleid-ontwikkelen-op-school/ and https://www.kennisnet.nl/stappenplan/werken-met-het-raamwerk-ai-geletterdheid/
prioritySummary: The plan principally aims to help primary and secondary schools create broadly supported AI policy that fits their educational vision and core values, enabling clear and considered decisions about AI use. It asks schools to weigh impacts on teaching, school operations, safety and professional development, and to clarify what teachers and students may do. Responsible and context-sensitive use is emphasized alongside attention to risks and public values such as justice, humanity and autonomy. The related AI-literacy guidance focuses on building school staff knowledge and skills for responsible use, with different proficiency levels depending on staff roles and school ambitions. The stated beneficiaries include the school community—staff and students, with parents and governance stakeholders involved in shaping the policy—not a single workforce or individual group. Evidence: https://www.kennisnet.nl/stappenplan/ai-beleid-ontwikkelen-op-school/ and https://www.kennisnet.nl/stappenplan/werken-met-het-raamwerk-ai-geletterdheid/
educationalTechnologySummary: The policy-plan page does not identify an AI product, learning platform, or software system as something Kennisnet develops or requires schools to use. It offers a downloadable example AI-policy document (DOCX) to adapt to a school’s circumstances. Related AI-literacy guidance provides a framework and compact framework (PDF), a self-evaluation (PDF), and a PowerPoint for organising a team session; these resources help schools assess staff development needs and plan professionalisation, rather than functioning as dedicated educational technology platforms. The inspected evidence therefore supports the use of downloadable digital documents and presentation materials, but does not establish that Kennisnet develops or uses an interactive AI-literacy technology. Evidence: https://www.kennisnet.nl/stappenplan/ai-beleid-ontwikkelen-op-school/ and https://www.kennisnet.nl/stappenplan/werken-met-het-raamwerk-ai-geletterdheid/

inclusion.reason: The initiative is issued by Kennisnet, an organization with significant reach in the Dutch educational sector (a national platform for schools), satisfying the 'system-scale adoption' inclusion route. The page explicitly mentions a 'six-step AI policy plan' and provides educational guidance on topics like ChatGPT, AI-tools, and their impact, fulfilling the mandatory AI-literacy requirement of providing educational content about how to use AI.
