metadata.Initiative / Programme: Proyecto de Ley para el buen uso y la gobernanza de la IA
metadata.Description: Bill approved by the Council of Ministers (May 2026) to implement the EU AI Act in Spain, designating supervisory authorities.

summary: Spain’s proposed Law on the Good Use and Governance of AI, approved by the Council of Ministers for submission to Congress, would adapt national law to the EU AI Act. It sets out supervisory authorities, compliance requirements and sanctions, and addresses public-sector AI use through measures including an inventory of systems and designated AI delegates. The bill also covers support for AI providers and calls for AI training and awareness-raising among public employees, though the announcement does not specify a curriculum or delivery approach.
pedagogicalSummary: The inspected announcement describes a proposed law, primarily a regulatory and governance measure, rather than a teaching programme. It says the law will promote training and awareness about AI among public employees, but gives no curriculum, teaching methods, learning activities, or delivery arrangements. Thus, employee training is an intended component, while the pedagogical approach cannot be established from this page; the limited evidence should not be taken to confirm that no further training design exists. Source: https://digital.gob.es/comunicacion/notas-prensa/mtdfp/2026/05/el-gobierno-aprueba-el-proyecto-de-ley-que-garantizara-una-super
prioritySummary: The bill’s main emphasis is establishing Spain’s governance and supervision framework for AI under the EU AI Act, with the stated aim of trustworthy use, human oversight, and protection of rights. It identifies supervisory authorities and sanctions, and adds public-sector measures such as an inventory of AI systems used in administrative procedures and an AI delegate. The announcement also presents safe innovation and support for AI providers as priorities, through controlled testing environments and measures to help them comply. It mentions training and awareness for public employees, but does not frame workforce upskilling as the bill’s principal purpose. Source: https://digital.gob.es/comunicacion/notas-prensa/mtdfp/2026/05/el-gobierno-aprueba-el-proyecto-de-ley-que-garantizara-una-super
educationalTechnologySummary: The announcement does not identify any educational platforms, software, hardware, or learning technologies developed or used for AI-literacy teaching. It describes AI sandboxes—controlled testing environments intended to help providers comply with legislation, including a national space to be operated by AESIA—but presents them as governance and innovation measures, not as educational tools. The page also mentions planned AI training and awareness for public employees without specifying technology used to deliver it. On the evidence inspected, therefore, no educational technology can be identified; this is a limit of the announcement, not proof that none exists elsewhere. Source: https://digital.gob.es/comunicacion/notas-prensa/mtdfp/2026/05/el-gobierno-aprueba-el-proyecto-de-ley-que-garantizara-una-super

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Estrategia de Inteligencia Artificial 2024
metadata.Description: Spanish government AI strategy (May 2024) structured in 3 axes/8 levers incl. the ALIA language models and public-sector AI.

summary: Estrategia de Inteligencia Artificial 2024 is Spain’s national government strategy for advancing AI across research, public services, business and society. It sets out three axes and eight levers, including investment in computing infrastructure, support for AI research and technology adoption, and development of language models such as ALIA. The strategy also identifies competency-building and training measures for school pupils and teachers, university learners, and adults, alongside initiatives for companies and public institutions. It is a policy framework rather than a standalone learning programme; the available evidence does not describe specific courses, instructional methods or learner materials.
pedagogicalSummary: The inspected pages do not provide evidence of a teaching or learning approach. The material presents an AI strategy rather than a learning programme: the accessible PDF text identifies the strategy and lists policy levers, including investment in supercomputing, while the ministry page describes its digital-policy remit. No learner activities, instructional methods, or learning organisation were visible in the inspected material. This is a limit of the accessible evidence, not confirmation that no related educational activity exists (https://portal.mineco.gob.es/es-es/digitalizacionIA/Documents/Estrategia_IA_2024.pdf; https://digital.gob.es/digitalizacion).
prioritySummary: The evidence points to a public-policy emphasis on advancing artificial intelligence and digitalisation, rather than a specifically educational objective. The PDF is titled “Estrategia de Inteligencia Artificial 2024” and its accessible contents list investment in supercomputing; the ministry page describes a remit to promote digitalisation across society and the economy while respecting individual and collective rights. The inspected text does not establish a more specific beneficiary hierarchy or show that AI literacy, workforce training, or individual well-being is the strategy’s principal aim (https://portal.mineco.gob.es/es-es/digitalizacionIA/Documents/Estrategia_IA_2024.pdf; https://digital.gob.es/digitalizacion).
educationalTechnologySummary: No educational technology is identified in the accessible material as being developed or used to support AI-literacy learning. The PDF’s visible contents mention investment in supercomputing, but do not describe it as a learning tool; the ministry page lists digital and AI policy areas without specifying learning platforms, software, or hardware. Because the PDF text could not be inspected in full, this is a limit of the available evidence, not confirmation that the initiative has no educational technologies (https://portal.mineco.gob.es/es-es/digitalizacionIA/Documents/Estrategia_IA_2024.pdf; https://digital.gob.es/digitalizacion).

inclusion.reason: The initiative meets the inclusion criterion under the government-issued route because it is a formal national strategy issued by a Spanish Ministry. It also contains clear AI-literacy–relevant educational content: it describes AI infrastructure, the role of GPUs, deep learning, research excellence criteria, and open-source hardware paradigms, which provide guidance on how AI works and can be used in research and innovation. Uncertainty: no specific standalone ‘AI literacy modules’ are explicitly listed as separate courses, but the document’s educational descriptions and calls to excellence satisfy the requirement for guidance on AI use.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: LOMLOE (Ley Orgánica 3/2020) – competence-based curriculum incl. digital competence
metadata.Description: Education law introducing competence-based curriculum incl. digital competence.

summary: LOMLOE (Organic Law 3/2020) reforms Spain’s education law and establishes a competence-based curriculum that includes digital competence. Its provisions govern school-age and adult education and address teachers and education-system implementation. The law’s broad digital-competence remit may encompass AI literacy, but the available evidence does not establish a specific AI focus, teaching method, or educational technology.
pedagogicalSummary: The initiative is a law modifying Spain’s education law, rather than a standalone teaching programme. The supplied description identifies a competence-based curriculum, including digital competence, but the inspected material does not establish how learning is taught or supported—for example, whether through projects, practice, or direct instruction. Competence-based curriculum is therefore the identifiable curricular orientation, not evidence for a particular classroom pedagogy. Further details about implementation were not established in this limited inspection. (https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2020-17264)
prioritySummary: The official page identifies Ley Orgánica 3/2020 as legislation modifying Spain’s education law. The supplied description characterizes its emphasis as introducing a competence-based curriculum that includes digital competence. This supports describing its priority as curricular reform and the inclusion of digital competence in education; the inspected material does not establish a more specific beneficiary group or a hierarchy among broader aims. Because this is a statutory measure, its aims should not be equated with evidence of particular teaching activities. (https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2020-17264)
educationalTechnologySummary: The inspected official page identifies the measure as a law modifying education legislation, and the supplied description refers to digital competence in the curriculum. Neither establishes that the initiative develops or uses a particular educational technology, platform, software, or hardware to support learning. Digital competence is a curricular subject or aim, not by itself evidence of a technology used for instruction. No educational technologies could be identified in the limited material inspected; this is a limit of the available evidence, not confirmation that none are used in implementation. (https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2020-17264)

inclusion.reason: Inclusion via the government mandate route: issued by the Spanish national government. Inclusion via AI literacy: mandates 'Digital Competence' in the curriculum, which includes understanding digital technologies and their societal impact, a requirement that encompasses AI literacy.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Plan Nacional de Competencias Digitales (2021)
metadata.Description: 2021 plan to raise citizens' basic digital skills, part of the Recovery, Transformation and Resilience Plan.

summary: Spain’s 2021 National Digital Skills Plan is a government initiative to improve digital skills and inclusion among the public and workforce. It sets policy priorities and provides a digital-competence framework, alongside an online self-assessment that offers users a report and learning recommendations and a catalogue of training activities from external providers. Its emphasis is broad digital competence, employment and lifelong learning rather than AI-specific literacy; the materials support self-directed assessment, but do not describe a particular classroom teaching method.
pedagogicalSummary: The inspected pages support a self-directed, diagnostic approach rather than a described classroom method. The online competency questionnaire assesses the user across 21 digital competencies, presenting increasingly difficult, context-based questions and estimating a level in each area. Users can review and download a report with learning recommendations, then use it to set a personal improvement plan. The site also points users to a searchable catalogue of training activities. The five-area competency model structures what is assessed, but does not itself specify a teaching method; the pages provide no clear evidence about instruction, facilitation, or classroom practice. These are digital-competence resources, not explicitly AI-literacy teaching. (https://generaciond.gob.es/cuestionario-competencial; https://generaciond.gob.es/iniciativas; https://generaciond.gob.es/plan-nacional)
prioritySummary: The stated priority is to build digital skills and inclusion among both workers and the wider public in Spain. The plan page links this to quality employment, reduced unemployment, greater productivity, and narrowing gender, social, and territorial divides. The Generación D Pact adds workforce and business aims: training people for digital competencies and employment, supporting SMEs and employees needing reskilling, and helping align digital talent with employers’ needs. It also emphasizes public awareness, collaboration among institutions and participating organizations, lifelong learning, and certification. The inspected pages therefore indicate several related priorities, rather than a single exclusive beneficiary or outcome. They describe broad digital competencies, not an AI-specific literacy priority. (https://generaciond.gob.es/plan-nacional; https://generaciond.gob.es/pacto-por-la-generacion-d)
educationalTechnologySummary: The site offers a web-based competency questionnaire as a learning-support tool: it assesses performance across digital-skill areas, saves progress for registered users, and provides a downloadable PDF report with links to learning recommendations. A searchable online catalogue lists training activities, including online and in-person options; the listings point to offerings from external providers, so the inspected pages do not establish that the plan develops or delivers those courses itself. The competency model is a framework, not an educational technology. No named learning-management platform, AI teaching tool, or hardware is identified in the inspected pages, and the initiative is presented as supporting broad digital competencies rather than specifically AI literacy. (https://generaciond.gob.es/cuestionario-competencial; https://generaciond.gob.es/iniciativas; https://generaciond.gob.es/plan-nacional)

inclusion.reason: The initiative is issued by the Spanish government (a national government entity), satisfying the inclusion route of government endorsement. It contains explicit educational content, structured learning levels, and competence domains with clear objectives for how users should develop digital skills, fulfilling the AI-literacy requirement (which in this case is about digital literacy broadly, but the initiative explicitly focuses on building competencies and includes guidance on using technology safely and creatively). The plan is not merely using AI to deliver education; rather, it provides educational frameworks, definitions of competencies, and guidance on digital tools. Therefore, it meets both the inclusion criteria and AI-literacy requirements.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: INTEF "Orientaciones para la integración de la IA en la formación del profesorado" (2026)
metadata.Description: INTEF document with principles and recommendations for ethical, effective integration of AI into initial and continuing teacher training.

summary: INTEF’s “Orientaciones para la integración de la IA en la formación del profesorado” is a Spanish Ministry of Education guidance document for teachers and organizations responsible for teacher training. It sets out principles and practical recommendations for integrating AI ethically and effectively into initial and continuing professional development, including a framework of five dimensions and three progression levels. Its emphasis is on developing teachers’ AI competencies and supporting critical, pedagogically meaningful use, alongside guidance, examples and methodological proposals for training providers. Equity, fundamental rights and responsible use are among its stated concerns; the available evidence does not describe a specific course format or AI tool.
pedagogicalSummary: The accessible article describes a proposed teacher-training approach rather than detailing a specific course or teaching method. It calls for training programmes that develop teachers’ AI competencies and help them apply AI critically and in pedagogically meaningful ways. The referenced guidance document is said to include examples, methodological proposals and resources, but the article does not explain the learning activities, sequence, delivery format, or how learning is assessed. It also recommends guidance and protocols for tutors, designers and participants in training activities. Thus, the evidence supports an emphasis on critical, pedagogy-connected professional learning, but not a more specific instructional model. Source: https://intef.es/Noticias/la-inteligencia-artificial-en-la-formacion-del-profesorado-un-compromiso-con-la-educacion-del-futuro/
prioritySummary: The initiative’s central emphasis is supporting teachers’ professional development, especially continuing training, so they can integrate AI effectively, critically and ethically into education. It also aims to support the organizations responsible for teacher training through practical recommendations, guidance and protocols. The article mentions administrative efficiency and informed decision-making as one strand of the proposed strategy, alongside developing teacher AI competencies and ensuring responsible use in training. Its main focus is data protection and digital rights, not AI literacy. Education provisions call for students to learn responsible, critical, and safe use of digital media, with attention to privacy and personal-data protection; the law does not specify teaching methods, learning materials, or educational technologies.

A specific pedagogical approach therefore cannot be identified; this is a limit of the evidence in the inspected legal text, not proof that no related educational practices exist. prioritySummary: The law’s broad purpose is protecting personal data and guaranteeing digital rights. It also calls for attention to digital inclusion, particularly for people at risk of exclusion. These provisions concern students and wider rights-holders, but the inspected source does not frame the initiative as an AI-literacy programme or establish a more specific AI-related priority. metadata.Initiative / Programme: ODITE report 2025 (personalised learning in primary through AI)
metadata.Description: Collective report by the Observatory of Educational Innovation and Digital Culture analysing AI's impact on personalised learning.

summary: The ODITE 2025 report is a collective analysis of how artificial intelligence may affect personalised learning, with a focus on primary education. Drawing on an analysis of 28 articles, it considers potential benefits and risks and argues that AI does not personalise learning on its own: educators’ decisions and pedagogical aims matter. It calls for ethical, democratic approaches that address inequality and protect pedagogical autonomy, and for education to foster critical citizenship. Published on the European Commission’s EPALE platform, the report does not specify a particular audience or instructional programme.
pedagogicalSummary: The accessible page describes a collective report and literature analysis, not a teaching programme with specified activities or a defined instructional method. It says the report assesses 28 articles through a content-validity index and discusses personalized learning, benefits, risks, and the need for deep pedagogical reflection. Its argument is that AI does not itself personalize education: educators’ decisions matter, and education should foster critical citizenship rather than focus only on measurable performance. These are principles advanced by the report, not evidence of a particular classroom pedagogy being implemented. The page does not provide further detail on how learners or teachers are taught or supported. (https://epale.ec.europa.eu/es/content/la-inteligencia-artificial-en-la-educacion-informe-odite-2025)
prioritySummary: The report’s central emphasis is to critically examine how AI may affect personalized learning in schools, teaching, and students, balancing potential benefits against risks. It cautions against assuming that adopting AI will solve educational problems, and highlights concerns about algorithmic control, corporate concentration, inequality, and loss of pedagogical autonomy. It calls for educational decisions grounded in ethical and democratic purposes and the common good, and for schools to promote critical citizenship beyond efficiency and measurable performance. The page presents these as the report’s priorities; it does not identify a specific learner group or workforce-upskilling goal as its primary beneficiary. (https://epale.ec.europa.eu/es/content/la-inteligencia-artificial-en-la-educacion-informe-odite-2025)
educationalTechnologySummary: The page discusses artificial intelligence broadly as a subject of the ODITE 2025 report, including its possible role in personalized learning, but it does not name any AI product, software, platform, hardware, or learning technology developed or used by the initiative. Nor does it describe technology-mediated learning activities. The report’s analysis of 28 articles is a research method, not an educational technology. Based on this page, whether the report or its authors use or develop specific educational technologies to support AI literacy cannot be established. (https://epale.ec.europa.eu/es/content/la-inteligencia-artificial-en-la-educacion-informe-odite-2025)

inclusion.reason: The initiative includes AI-literacy elements as it provides educational content and analysis regarding AI's impact on learning (satisfying the 'educational content' requirement). It satisfies an inclusion route because it is issued via the European Commission's official platform (epale.ec.europa.eu), making it a resource from an intergovernmental body.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Study on the impact of AI on education in Spain (Observatorio de la Infancia)
metadata.Description: Study referenced via Observatorio de la Infancia document record.

summary: A research study by Empantallados and GAD3, documented by Spain’s Observatory for Childhood, examines how families, adolescents aged 14–17, and non-university teachers use and perceive AI in education. Based on a representative survey conducted in late 2023, it discusses educational uses, responsible-use guidance, privacy, reliability, creativity, and views on future employment. It is a report rather than a teaching programme, and the evidence does not establish a specific instructional approach or learning technology.
pedagogicalSummary: The inspected pages describe a research study, not a teaching programme: its method is a survey of parents, 14–17-year-olds and non-university teachers in Spain, so no instructional sequence or learner-support model is established. The study does call for families and teachers to guide minors in learning about AI and using it responsibly, and reports views on AI for finding information or explaining class content. These are recommendations and perceived uses, not evidence that the study itself delivers those learning activities. Accordingly, a specific pedagogical approach cannot be identified from the accessible evidence (https://www.observatoriodelainfancia.es/oia/esp/documentos_ficha.aspx?id=8555; https://www.observatoriodelainfancia.es/oia/esp/descargar.aspx?id=8555&tipo=documento).
prioritySummary: The study principally aims to document how families, adolescents and non-university teachers in Spain use and perceive AI in education, based on a representative survey conducted in late 2023. Its findings highlight a need for clear educational guidance from families and teachers so minors can learn about AI and use it responsibly; they also address privacy, reliability, creativity and possible school-related benefits. The evidence therefore points to understanding and supporting young people’s AI use, with family and school involvement, rather than a programme focused mainly on workforce upskilling or a single policy outcome. The study also reports adults’ views about future work, but that is one topic among several (https://www.observatoriodelainfancia.es/oia/esp/documentos_ficha.aspx?id=8555; https://empantallados.com/ia/).
educationalTechnologySummary: The inspected pages do not identify an educational technology developed or deployed by the study as a learning intervention. Instead, the report surveys use of AI tools, especially ChatGPT, and reports that respondents see possible school-related uses in searching for information, explaining class content, generating teachers’ lesson ideas and supplementing subject content. These are reported uses and opinions, not evidence that the initiative supplies or integrates those tools. Empantallados describes itself as a digital platform offering articles, expert interviews and downloadable resources for parents, but the inspected study page does not establish that these resources teach AI literacy or that a specific platform, software or hardware supports the study’s learning (https://www.observatoriodelainfancia.es/oia/esp/documentos_ficha.aspx?id=8555; https://empantallados.com/ia/).

inclusion.reason: The initiative qualifies for inclusion under the 'Government' route as it is issued by the Observatory for Childhood (Observatorio de la Infancia), a public observatory associated with the Andalusian government. Although the specific page describes only a research study rather than a curriculum or guide, the document addresses AI in education and meets the government inclusion criteria; uncertainty remains regarding whether the full content contains direct educational modules explaining how AI works, but this is not excluded as it may be a standalone publication within the broader AI literacy context.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Competència digital docent en intel·ligència artificial (Catalonia, Dec 2025)
metadata.Description: Catalan framework defining knowledge, skills and attitudes teachers need for ethical, reflective AI use.

summary: Competència digital docent en intel·ligència artificial is a guide and competence framework published by Catalonia’s Department of Education and Vocational Training for teachers. It outlines knowledge, skills and attitudes for responsible, critical and ethical use of AI in educational settings, complementing Catalonia’s existing teacher digital competence framework. The guide calls for ongoing training, pedagogical support and resources, but does not specify a course structure or particular teaching methods.
pedagogicalSummary: The initiative is presented as a living, orienting guide to help teachers develop the competence to use AI in educational contexts. The page says implementation should be supported by continuous training, pedagogical accompaniment and resources, and should be didactically relevant, ethical and consistent with current rules. This indicates ongoing professional learning with support, but the inspected page does not describe a specific teaching method, course structure, classroom activity or assessment approach. The stated supports are therefore not evidence of a particular pedagogy. Further detail may be in the linked document, whose contents were not available in the inspected page. Source: https://educacio.gencat.cat/ca/departament/publicacions/monografies/mon-digital/competencia-digital-docent-intelligencia-artificial/index.html
prioritySummary: The initiative principally aims to build teachers’ professional competence for responsible and critical use of AI in education, complementing Catalonia’s existing digital competence framework for teachers. It seeks to make implementation pedagogically relevant, ethical, technically viable and compliant with current rules, while supporting teachers’ professional development through training, accompaniment and resources. The page also connects this teacher-focused capacity-building to a broader societal benefit: a digitally conscious citizenry equipped to meet current and future challenges with judgment, creativity and responsibility. It does not establish a more specific priority among these aims. Source: https://educacio.gencat.cat/ca/departament/publicacions/monografies/mon-digital/competencia-digital-docent-intelligencia-artificial/index.html
educationalTechnologySummary: The page identifies generative AI as a widely used, general-purpose technology whose effects motivate the initiative, and describes responsible, critical AI use as a competence for teachers. However, the inspected material does not name any AI product, learning platform, software or hardware that the initiative develops or uses to support learning. Nor does it establish that generative AI itself is deployed as an instructional tool by the initiative; here it is described as the subject of teacher competence and educational change. The page mentions resources to support implementation but does not specify their technological form. The linked guide may provide more detail, but its contents were not available in the inspected page. Source: https://educacio.gencat.cat/ca/departament/publicacions/monografies/mon-digital/competencia-digital-docent-intelligencia-artificial/index.html

metadata.Initiative / Programme: "La intel·ligència artificial en l'educació" – orientations (Dept. d'Educació, Catalonia, 2024)
metadata.Description: Catalan Department of Education 2024 recommendations for critical, responsible incorporation of AI in schools.

summary: La intel·ligència artificial en l’educació is a 2024 publication from Catalonia’s Department of Education and Vocational Training offering orientations and recommendations for using AI in schools. Aimed at teachers and school staff, it encourages reflection on AI’s educational opportunities, challenges and uncertainties, with an emphasis on critical and responsible use. It is guidance rather than a course or specified instructional programme, and does not identify particular AI tools or platforms. Catalan and English versions are available.
pedagogicalSummary: The accessible page describes guidance intended to foster reflection among teachers and school staffrooms (“claustres”) about AI’s educational opportunities, challenges, and unresolved questions. This supports a reflective, discussion-oriented approach for educators, but the page does not describe lessons, learner activities, training formats, or a specific teaching methodology. The document is presented as orientations and recommendations for use in schools, not as a course or instructional programme. Because the linked guidance document itself was not accessible in the inspected page text, further pedagogical detail cannot be confirmed. Source: https://educacio.gencat.cat/ca/departament/publicacions/monografies/mon-digital/intelligencia-artificial-educacio/
prioritySummary: The initiative’s stated emphasis is to consider and guide the use of AI in education: the Department says it formed a working group to monitor the technology’s use and assess educational applications, and that its document aims to prompt educators’ reflection on opportunities, challenges, doubts, and uncertainties. The immediate audience identified is teachers and school staffrooms; the broader intended beneficiary is school education, through informed consideration of AI applications. metadata.Initiative / Programme: Llibre blanc d'educació i llengua (Catalonia, 2023)
metadata.Description: 2023 CIDAI (Catalonia.AI) white paper analysing how AI can address challenges in education and the Catalan language sector.

summary: The 2023 Llibre blanc d’educació i llengua is a CIDAI (Catalonia.AI) white paper examining AI adoption in Catalonia’s education and Catalan-language sectors. Aimed at sector stakeholders, it considers challenges, opportunities, and potential applications, and frames education through learning with AI, learning about AI, and preparing for AI. It offers sector-level analysis and guidance rather than a described learner-facing course or instructional programme.
pedagogicalSummary: The inspected pages present this initiative as a white paper analysing AI in education and the Catalan language, not as a teaching or learner-facing programme. They do not describe a learning sequence, instructional method, or learner support. CIDAI says its white papers generally involve sector value-chain representatives and examine barriers, opportunities, and illustrative applications, but the available description does not specify how this process was applied to this report. Thus, no pedagogical approach can be identified from the inspected evidence; this is a lack of described teaching activity, not evidence that the full document contains none. Sources: https://cidai.eu/llibres-blancs/ and https://cdn.eurecat.org/PDF/CIDAI/Llibre-blanc-Educacio-i-Llengua.pdf
prioritySummary: The stated emphasis is to encourage AI adoption and incorporation in Catalonia’s education sector while examining the importance of AI applications for the Catalan language. These are presented as connected aims; the inspected description does not establish that one takes precedence. The intended benefit is therefore framed at the sector and language level, rather than as an explicit programme for individual learners or workforce training. CIDAI describes its white papers as analysing AI adoption in relevant sectors of the Catalan economy, including sector barriers, opportunities, and application examples. The PDF’s accessible title likewise frames the report around AI applied to education and language and responding to challenges in both areas. The PDF text available in this inspection was limited, so further priorities in the report cannot be confirmed. Sources: https://cidai.eu/llibres-blancs/ and https://cdn.eurecat.org/PDF/CIDAI/Llibre-blanc-Educacio-i-Llengua.pdf
educationalTechnologySummary: The inspected pages identify no educational technology, platform, software, or hardware developed or used by the initiative to support learning. The white paper is described as analysing AI applications in education and their importance for Catalan, but discussing AI as a subject or potential application does not establish that a specific technology is deployed as a learning tool. CIDAI’s general description says its white papers are complemented by projects illustrating use cases and applications, but the accessible listing does not identify any such educational tool for this report. The PDF extraction exposed its title but not enough of its contents to assess whether it names specific technologies. Accordingly, no educational technology can be confirmed from the inspected evidence; that is an evidence limitation, not confirmation that none is discussed in the full report. Sources: https://cidai.eu/llibres-blancs/ and https://cdn.eurecat.org/PDF/CIDAI/Llibre-blanc-Educacio-i-Llengua.pdf

inclusion.reason: The initiative is issued by CIDAI (Catalonia.AI), a public body of the Catalan government, which satisfies the inclusion route for sub-national government endorsement. It includes explicit educational content about AI literacy, referencing the UNESCO framework of learning with/about AI and preparing for AI, and it is published as a white paper intended to guide the education and language sector in Catalonia rather than being a single-institution product or tool-only offering.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Catalonia.AI – AI strategy of Catalonia
metadata.Description: Catalan government strategy to boost the AI ecosystem, research, talent, adoption and ethics, including the 2030 update.

summary: Catalonia.AI is the Government of Catalonia’s strategy for developing the region’s AI ecosystem, including research and innovation, talent, business adoption, and responsible use. Its learning offer includes CiutadanIA, a course for the public on basic AI concepts, everyday applications, and safe and ethical use; CIDAI masterclasses and other specialized training for professionals and organizations; and OEIAC seminars on ethics, social impacts, and legal compliance. The described formats include courses, expert-led masterclasses, and seminars, but the available information does not specify instructional technologies or detailed teaching methods.
pedagogicalSummary: The inspected page describes several learning formats but gives limited detail about their instructional design. CiutadanIA is a course covering basic AI concepts, recognizing AI in everyday life, safe interaction, and practical support within ethical frameworks. CIDAI offers specialized training through masterclasses led by member organizations, while OEIAC's seminar series addresses ethics, social impact, and legal compliance. The page also points to a collection of existing training proposals for businesses, organizations, and professionals. metadata.Initiative / Programme: FECC AI Framework Protocol (2025) & guidelines (Catalonia)
metadata.Description: Fundació Escola Cristiana de Catalunya protocol for school AI policies and guidelines for the school community.

summary: Fundació Escola Cristiana de Catalunya’s digital-education expert group provides an AI framework protocol and practical guidance to help affiliated schools develop context-sensitive policies for responsible AI use. Its materials address teachers, school leaders, administrative staff, students and families, and include an IRIS framework, infographics and an informed-consent template. The approach emphasizes ethical, safe and critical use, with school-level reflection and collaborative planning rather than a specified classroom AI-literacy method. FECC also describes sharing expert-group resources through training and professional exchange; the page identifies nearly 400 affiliated schools as potential beneficiaries but does not establish uptake.
pedagogicalSummary: The inspected page does not describe a specific classroom teaching method for AI literacy. For AI, the digital experts’ group is tasked with exploring ethical, effective and pedagogically enriching integration, and its framework is intended to help schools develop their own protocols through reflection and consensual work. More generally, FECC says its expert groups share practical materials through training sessions, conferences and exchanges of experience, which schools can adapt to their needs. This is evidence of professional support and collaborative school-level planning, not a description of how students are taught about AI. The page’s references to active, manipulative mathematics learning concern a different expert group and are not evidence of an AI pedagogy. (https://www.fecc.cat/grups-experts-ambit-pedagogic/)
prioritySummary: The initiative’s stated emphasis is to help FECC-affiliated schools make responsible, context-sensitive decisions about AI use. The framework offers considerations and the FECC position so schools can develop their own use and regulation protocols; accompanying recommendations address teachers, leadership teams, administrative staff, students and families. The stated broader aim is to foster a critical, safe and responsible digital culture in schools. The page identifies nearly 400 affiliated schools as the intended beneficiaries of the expert groups’ practical resources, while the AI materials specifically address the wider school community. It does not establish a separate workforce or personal well-being priority, nor does it rank the different stakeholder benefits. (https://www.fecc.cat/grups-experts-ambit-pedagogic/)
educationalTechnologySummary: The page says the digital experts’ group explores integrating educational technology and AI, but does not identify particular AI products or platforms used for instruction. It lists an “Escala IRIS” framework for educational AI use, an “Infografia Escala IRIS,” and a “Generador IRIS” among the group’s resources. The page does not explain the generator’s technical form, who developed it, whether it is a software tool, or how learners or educators use it to support learning. The protocol, recommendations, consent template and infographics are identified as materials, not as learning technologies. Thus the page provides names of potentially relevant resources but insufficient detail to establish the development or classroom use of specific educational technologies. (https://www.fecc.cat/grups-experts-ambit-pedagogic/)

inclusion.reason: The page describes AI-use guidance for multiple school-community groups, which meets the AI-literacy requirement by addressing how to use AI responsibly. It says FECC serves nearly 400 affiliated schools and shares materials with them; this suggests reach beyond a single institution, though actual uptake and implementation are not established. No government endorsement is stated. Source: https://www.fecc.cat/grups-experts-ambit-pedagogic/

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Orientacions per a l'ús de la IA als centres educatius (Catalonia, Sept 2026)
metadata.Description: Catalan guidelines for students, teachers, schools and families, incl. age limits and rules for documented AI use.

summary: The Catalan Department of Education’s XTEC initiative provides guidance on AI use in educational centres for students, teachers, schools and families. Its recommendations address educational opportunities and challenges, responsible and critical use, age-related considerations, and documenting AI use. Related site materials offer teacher training in using generative AI and designing learning activities and assessments, alongside curated resources and classroom examples. The evidence supports a practical, reflective approach, but does not establish a single overarching pedagogy or a specific AI platform provided by the initiative.
pedagogicalSummary: The initiative’s accessible pages show a mix of guidance and professional learning, rather than a single stated teaching method. The guidance document is presented as identifying AI’s educational opportunities and challenges, while the training offers practical and reflective learning for teachers: participants practise interacting with AI, consider classroom integration, and learn to design activities and assessment. A course also describes co-creating learning situations with generative AI. The classroom-experience section collects examples from different school stages, but the inspected page provides little detail on how those activities are taught. Thus, practice, reflection, and activity design are supported by the evidence; a more specific overarching pedagogy is not established. Sources: https://projectes.xtec.cat/ia/general/orientacions-i-recomanacions-per-lus-de-la-intelligencia-artificial-als-centres-educatius/ ; https://projectes.xtec.cat/ia/formacio/ ; https://projectes.xtec.cat/ia/a-les-aules/experiencies-aula/
prioritySummary: The initiative is principally concerned with helping the education community understand and use AI in schools, with particular evidence of support for teachers and school practice. Its guidance aims to track AI’s use in education and set out opportunities, challenges, and unresolved questions. The training focuses on applying generative AI to educational content creation, personalization, assessment, and responsible classroom use; other courses offer strategies for integrating AI into teaching and teaching students to use it. The site also collects classroom experiences involving both students and teachers. The inspected pages therefore indicate educational improvement and responsible school use as priorities, alongside teacher capability-building; they do not establish a separate societal or individual-well-being priority. Sources: https://projectes.xtec.cat/ia/general/orientacions-i-recomanacions-per-lus-de-la-intelligencia-artificial-als-centres-educatius/ ; https://projectes.xtec.cat/ia/formacio/ ; https://projectes.xtec.cat/ia/a-les-aules/experiencies-aula/
educationalTechnologySummary: The inspected pages do not identify a proprietary educational technology, learning platform, or hardware developed by the initiative. The site provides guidance, training information, and a resource repository. Training describes learning to interact with AI and using generative AI for educational content, personalized learning, assessment, and classroom activities, but does not specify which software participants use. The guidance page mentions ChatGPT as a catalyst for attention to AI in education, not as a platform the initiative provides. The repository lists external tools and materials, including Jan.ai and an educational prompt GPT, but the accessible descriptions attribute these to outside creators; they should not be treated as technologies developed by the initiative. The evidence supports a resource-curation and training role, but does not establish a particular AI tool used in its courses. Sources: https://projectes.xtec.cat/ia/general/orientacions-i-recomanacions-per-lus-de-la-intelligencia-artificial-als-centres-educatius/ ; https://projectes.xtec.cat/ia/formacio/ ; https://projectes.xtec.cat/ia/recursos-repo/

inclusion.reason: The initiative includes AI literacy through explicit educational guidance on how AI works, its applications, risks (bias, data protection), and how to use it critically in learning contexts (e.g., prompt engineering exercises, evaluation of AI-generated content). It is issued by XTEC, a public Catalan education authority (part of the Department of Education of the Government of Catalonia), satisfying the national/sub-national government inclusion route. The document provides structured educational content on AI competence, civic skills related to AI, and practical classroom use cases.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Pla d'Educació Digital de Catalunya
metadata.Description: Catalan government plan to build digital competences of students and teachers, including AI-related skills, across Catalonia's schools.

summary: The Pla d’Educació Digital de Catalunya is a Catalan government plan (2020–2023) to strengthen digital competence among students, teachers and educational centres and support the wider use of technology in education. Its actions include centre transformation, training and advisory support, and guidance and materials. The initiative is described as including AI-related learning, but the available page emphasizes digital competence broadly and does not detail AI teaching methods or tools.
pedagogicalSummary: The inspected page describes a strategic plan, not a specific teaching method: it aims to develop digital competences and improve the digital competence of students, teachers and schools as part of educational transformation. It does not explain how learning is organised, what classroom activities are used, or how learning is supported, so no particular pedagogy can be identified from this evidence. The page also does not specifically describe AI-literacy teaching. This is a limit of the inspected information, not evidence that the broader plan has no pedagogical activities. Source: https://educacio.gencat.cat/ca/departament/linies-estrategiques/pla-educacio-digital/
prioritySummary: The plan’s stated emphasis is building digital competence among Catalonia’s citizens, especially students, teachers and educational centres, so they can live and work in a society undergoing rapid technology-driven change. It also seeks to position Catalonia as a leading country in educational use of technology, linking that ambition to educational and social success and to broader educational transformation. These are related aims; the page does not establish a hierarchy among them. Although the initiative description refers to AI-related skills, the inspected page frames its objectives broadly around digital competence and does not specify AI as a priority. Source: https://educacio.gencat.cat/ca/departament/linies-estrategiques/pla-educacio-digital/
educationalTechnologySummary: The page presents educational use of technology as a strategic goal, but does not identify any particular platform, software, device, or other educational technology that the plan develops or uses to support learning. It mentions accompanying areas such as centre transformation, training and advisory support, and guidance and materials, without describing their technological components. The website itself is an information source and is not evidence that a specific technology is used for teaching. No AI tool or technology for AI literacy is identified in the inspected page; whether such tools are described elsewhere in the plan remains unclear. Source: https://educacio.gencat.cat/ca/departament/linies-estrategiques/pla-educacio-digital/

inclusion.reason: The initiative qualifies for inclusion because it is formally issued and mandated by a sub-national government (the Catalan Government), meeting the first Inclusion Route criterion regardless of whether additional scale evidence is needed. The site contains educational content and learning objectives focused on digital competences, including specific sections on Artificial Intelligence skills and how to use AI tools in education, satisfying the AI-literacy requirement.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: URV guidelines on generative AI in teaching
metadata.Description: URV guide series helping faculty understand and critically integrate generative AI into teaching practice.

summary: Universitat Rovira i Virgili’s guide series supports university teaching staff in understanding and integrating generative AI into teaching. It offers practical suggestions for using tools such as ChatGPT in learning activities and teaching tasks, while encouraging students to check and discuss AI outputs, disclose their use, and consider ethical and social implications. The guidance also addresses curriculum, assessment, academic integrity, and responsible use; it recommends third-party tools rather than describing a dedicated AI technology developed by the initiative.
pedagogicalSummary: The guide presents practical, activity-based learning rather than a single formal teaching model. It suggests using ChatGPT as an information source or as one step in a student’s work, then having students check, revise, compare, justify, or debate its output using course content and credible references. Examples include identifying errors in generated code, evaluating true and false claims, debating the chatbot, and practising languages. Students are asked to disclose and cite their AI use and to consider bias and ethical and social consequences. The assessment guidance also recommends following students’ work in stages, valuing process and ongoing feedback, and using portfolios or oral checks. These are recommendations for instructors, not evidence that the initiative itself delivers courses. Evidence: https://docs.campusvirtual.urv.cat/wiki/Per_qu%C3%A8_i_com_incorporar_la_IA_en_les_activitats_d%E2%80%99aprenentatge_dels_estudiants.; https://docs.campusvirtual.urv.cat/wiki/Impacte_de_la_IA_en_l%E2%80%99avaluaci%C3%B3.
prioritySummary: The initiative’s immediate purpose is to help URV faculty begin integrating AI into teaching, including curriculum, teaching tasks, student activities, and assessment. Its broader educational emphasis is preparing students to use AI in professional fields where it is increasingly present, while developing AI literacy, critical thinking, and awareness of ethical and social effects. The guidance highlights human rights, equality, inclusion, bias, privacy, the digital divide, and academic integrity; it also frames AI as a teaching aid rather than a replacement for educators. The inspected pages therefore indicate connected priorities—faculty support, student preparation, and responsible critical engagement—without establishing that one of these is the sole or overriding goal. Evidence: https://docs.campusvirtual.urv.cat/wiki/IA_i_doc%C3%A8ncia._Una_guia_pel_professorat_URV.; https://docs.campusvirtual.urv.cat/wiki/Afectacions_de_la_IA_en_el_curr%C3%ADculum.
educationalTechnologySummary: The inspected pages do not identify a dedicated educational technology developed by the initiative. Instead, they recommend that instructors and students use external generative-AI products as resources in teaching and learning activities. ChatGPT is the most prominent example, suggested for generating and discussing text, questions, cases, code, and other outputs; DALL-E, Rephrase.ai, and Synthesia are mentioned as possible tools for producing instructional images or video. The guide says the URV Campus Virtual is based on Moodle, but describes AI integration into Moodle as a possibility being explored, not as a deployed URV learning feature. Thus the evidence supports recommended use of third-party tools, not development or confirmed implementation of an AI-enabled platform by the initiative. metadata.Initiative / Programme: Edugalia (Galicia)
metadata.Description: Galician government project (€16.5m) applying AI to educational management, early warning and reducing school dropout.

summary: EdugalIA is a Xunta de Galicia project to develop an integrated digital ecosystem for educational management and student support. Planned components include a unified academic record and access portal for students, families and schools, alongside data analytics, predictive dropout-risk alerts, scenario simulation and AI-based virtual assistants. The project aims to support earlier, more personalised attention and improve administrative decisions and resource allocation. It is an education-system initiative rather than a described AI-literacy curriculum; its research and development and later deployment are planned for 2026–2030.
pedagogicalSummary: The inspected coverage describes EdugalIA chiefly as a digital education-management and student-support project, not as an AI-literacy teaching programme. It gives no evidence of a teaching method, curriculum, or organised learning activities for students or staff, so no pedagogical approach can be established from these pages. The project is intended to help identify students at risk of leaving school and enable more personalised educational attention; that is a support goal, not evidence of a particular pedagogy. The article notes that pedagogues joined a multidisciplinary advisory team that helped define indicators, system architecture, and ethical principles, but does not describe their role in teaching. These details come from https://galiciaxa.com/es/news/la-xunta-lanza-edugalia-el-mayor-proyecto-de-ia-educativa-en-espana/111467/ and its Galician counterpart, https://galiciaxa.com/news/a-xunta-inicia-edugalia-o-maior-proxecto-de-ia-educativa-de-espana/111467/.
prioritySummary: EdugalIA’s stated emphasis is improving educational outcomes and public education management in Galicia: the project aims to improve school success, reduce educational dropout, and help schools and administrators make decisions and allocate resources. Its planned analysis of integrated data is meant to identify risk factors and students needing earlier or more personalised attention, as well as schools that may require additional resources. The initiative also prioritises making educational information and administrative interaction accessible to students and families through a unified academic record and shared access point. The article does not establish a separate workforce-upskilling or general AI-literacy objective. These priorities are described at https://galiciaxa.com/es/news/la-xunta-lanza-edugalia-el-mayor-proyecto-de-ia-educativa-en-espana/111467/; the Galician-language account is https://galiciaxa.com/news/a-xunta-inicia-edugalia-o-maior-proxecto-de-ia-educativa-de-espana/111467/.
educationalTechnologySummary: The article says EdugalIA is being designed as an integrated digital ecosystem, with research and development preceding planned deployment; it does not report that these tools are already in operation. Identified components include advanced data analytics, predictive analysis to detect dropout risk, early-warning systems, scenario simulation, and AI-based virtual assistants. The project also plans a platform for academic information, a single digital academic record covering a student’s educational trajectory, and a shared access and interaction space for students, families, schools, and the Xunta. These are described as supporting risk detection, resource decisions, personalised attention, information access, and administrative tasks. No named commercial software, hardware, or external platform is specified. Sources: https://galiciaxa.com/es/news/la-xunta-lanza-edugalia-el-mayor-proyecto-de-ia-educativa-en-espana/111467/ and https://galiciaxa.com/news/a-xunta-inicia-edugalia-o-maior-proxecto-de-ia-educativa-de-espana/111467/.

inclusion.reason: It satisfies the inclusion route through formal issuance and substantial government funding by the Xunta de Galicia; while explicit AI literacy curriculum components are not described in this excerpt, the involvement of pedagogues implies educational integration appropriate for inclusion in an AI-literacy screening.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Estratexia de Educación Dixital 2030 (Galicia)
metadata.Description: Galician digital education strategy 2030.

summary: Estratexia de Educación Dixital 2030 is the Galician Government’s strategy for developing digital education across the region through 2030. It addresses educational centres and school-age learners, includes teacher training, and is reported to cover AI literacy topics such as machine learning, deepfakes and disinformation. The available evidence establishes its strategic, regional scope but provides limited detail on specific teaching methods, technologies, materials or implementation.
pedagogicalSummary: The accessible opening of the PDF identifies the document as Galicia’s Digital Education Strategy 2030 and shows a contents page with sections on its vision and strategic foundations. Those pages do not describe teaching activities, instructional methods, or how learning is organised or supported. The strategy may address these topics later in the document, but they could not be established from the readable inspection; this is a limit of the accessible evidence, not confirmation that the initiative has no pedagogical approach. Source: https://www.edu.xunta.gal/portal/sites/web/files/estratexia_dixital_2030_ok.pdf
prioritySummary: The title identifies the initiative’s broad emphasis as digital education in Galicia through 2030. However, the readable material was limited to the cover and the start of the contents, so it does not establish the strategy’s specific objectives, intended beneficiaries, or whether it prioritises learners, educators, institutions, or wider societal outcomes. A more specific account of its priorities is therefore uncertain from the inspected evidence. Source: https://www.edu.xunta.gal/portal/sites/web/files/estratexia_dixital_2030_ok.pdf
educationalTechnologySummary: The readable portion of the strategy does not identify any educational technology, platform, software, or hardware that the initiative develops or uses to support learning. Its title concerns digital education, but that alone does not establish use of particular technologies as learning tools. Because the PDF’s extracted text was too large to inspect beyond its opening and contents, no conclusion can be drawn about whether technologies are described elsewhere in the strategy. Source: https://www.edu.xunta.gal/portal/sites/web/files/estratexia_dixital_2030_ok.pdf

inclusion.reason: The initiative qualifies for inclusion because it is issued by the Galician Government (sub-national government body) and includes explicit AI literacy educational content such as combating disinformation/deepfakes, understanding AI technologies like machine learning, and teacher training on these topics.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Galician framework for teachers' digital competence
metadata.Description: Galician framework, based on EU DigComp, regulating accreditation of teachers' digital competences including AI-related skills.

summary: The Xunta de Galicia’s Galician Digital Competence Framework adapts the European DigComp model to define and certify digital skills across personal, professional, educational and civic contexts. The regional initiative prepares EGAP and CeMIT trainers to support learning and certification for citizens and public employees, including through an online self-training course and a launch event with remote access. AI-related skills are included, but the available evidence does not establish AI literacy as a distinct priority or describe specific AI-focused teaching methods or tools.
pedagogicalSummary: The accessible account describes a train-the-trainer model: EGAP tutors and CeMIT network ICT agents receive ComDix training so they can later teach digital competencies and support related certification for citizens and public employees. The initial event introduced the framework, included a question-and-answer session, and was followed by an online self-training course and a planned in-person final exam. This supports a combination of self-directed online study, an introductory group session, and assessment, but the inspected pages do not explain course activities, instructional methods, or any AI-specific pedagogy. The framework itself defines competencies rather than a teaching method. (https://amtega.xunta.gal/es/noticia/la-xunta-pone-en-marcha-el-marco-gallego-de-competencias-digitales-con-la-jornada-inaugural)
prioritySummary: The initiative aims to establish a Galician digital-competence framework and tiered certification, while preparing trainers to deliver learning and accreditation to both the public and public-sector employees. Its scope is broader than teachers: the framework covers personal, professional, educational, and civic contexts. The linked digital-competence overview also emphasizes inclusive access, greater confidence and capability in digital life, improved quality of life and work opportunities, and reducing digital divides, especially for vulnerable groups. The evidence therefore indicates several related priorities—skills and recognition, inclusive participation, and empowerment—rather than a single narrow workforce objective. The inspected pages do not establish a distinct AI-literacy priority. (https://amtega.xunta.gal/es/noticia/la-xunta-pone-en-marcha-el-marco-gallego-de-competencias-digitales-con-la-jornada-inaugural; https://amtega.xunta.gal/es/tematica/competencias-digitales)
educationalTechnologySummary: The inspected announcement identifies no named learning platform, software, hardware, or AI tool developed by the initiative. It does report an online self-training course, “ComDix Iniciación,” for trainers and a livestream of the launch event to enable remote participation; these are evidence of online delivery, but the platform or technical implementation is not specified. The Red CeMIT is identified as a collaborating network whose trainers will teach and support certification, not as a particular educational technology. The wider framework and its certification are competency and accreditation structures, not technologies. Thus, the available evidence supports use of online course delivery and streaming, but not the identification of a specific educational technology product. (https://amtega.xunta.gal/es/noticia/la-xunta-pone-en-marcha-el-marco-gallego-de-competencias-digitales-con-la-jornada-inaugural)

inclusion.reason: This initiative qualifies for inclusion under two routes: First, it is issued by a sub-national government (the Xunta de Galicia), satisfying the 'government endorsement' requirement regardless of AI literacy. Second, the page explicitly states the framework regulates accreditation of teachers' digital competences 'including AI-related skills,' confirming the presence of educational content and learning objectives about AI use/understanding, which fulfills the AI-literacy requirement.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: CEFIRE d'Intel·ligència Artificial i Pensament Computacional (Valencia, 2025)
metadata.Description: Specialised teacher-training centre in La Nucia (Alicante) created in 2025 to train Valencian teachers in AI and computational thinking.

summary: CEFIRE d’Intel·ligència Artificial i Pensament Computacional is a specialised teacher-training centre established in 2025 by the Valencian education authorities. It provides professional learning for teachers across education stages and supports schools in planning, implementing and evaluating projects involving artificial intelligence, computational thinking, programming and robotics. Its offerings include training on practical and pedagogical uses of AI, alongside related resources; the available information describes project-oriented support but does not specify a particular teaching method or course format.
pedagogicalSummary: The accessible page describes a teacher-training programme and support for schools, but does not specify a detailed teaching method or the format of its courses. It says the centre coordinates training actions with other CEFIRE centres and advises schools on planning, implementing and evaluating didactic projects. This supports describing its approach as professional learning linked to practical school projects; the page also promotes pedagogical practices responsive to current and future challenges. It mentions creativity and cooperation as part of its work, but does not explain how these are enacted in learning activities. The page therefore supports a broad account of project-oriented teacher support, not a claim about a particular instructional model. Source: https://portal.edu.gva.es/cefire/xarxa-cefire/cfr_cefire-ia/
prioritySummary: The initiative’s clearest emphasis is professional development for teachers across all stages of education in the Valencian Community, alongside direct support for schools. It aims to build teachers’ capacity in computational thinking, artificial intelligence, programming, robotics and related technologies, and to help schools plan, implement and evaluate didactic projects in these areas. The page also frames this work as contributing to educational digital transformation and preparing students for a changing society, so learners and broader societal readiness are stated as downstream benefits. It does not identify workforce upskilling beyond education, individual well-being, or another priority as a principal aim. The inspected page establishes these broad goals but gives no further evidence about how priorities are ranked. Source: https://portal.edu.gva.es/cefire/xarxa-cefire/cfr_cefire-ia/
educationalTechnologySummary: The inspected page identifies artificial intelligence, computational thinking, programming, robotics and related technologies as subjects of the centre’s training plan, but does not name specific software, hardware or platforms used or developed to support learning. It lists “Recursos CEFIRE IA i PC” and provides an “Accés a Aules” link, but the page does not describe the resources, explain Aules’ role in this initiative, or show how either supports learning; their presence alone is insufficient to establish a specific educational-technology use. Thus, no particular learning technology can be confidently identified from the inspected material. This is a limit of the accessible evidence, not confirmation that the centre uses or develops none. Source: https://portal.edu.gva.es/cefire/xarxa-cefire/cfr_cefire-ia/

inclusion.reason: The initiative includes clear AI literacy elements through dedicated training modules on using AI tools, integrating AI in education, and developing computational thinking skills. It is formally endorsed by the Valencian government (Conselleria d'Educació), which satisfies the inclusion route of being issued or funded by a sub-national government. The centre operates as part of a network of CEFIRE training centres across Valencia, suggesting institutional backing and potential wider reach within the region.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: Generalitat Valenciana digital education plan
metadata.Description: Valencian education department's strategic plans page covering digital transformation and technology roadmap for schools.

summary: The Generalitat Valenciana’s 2024–2028 digital education plan is a regional strategy to modernise education and promote inclusive, accessible, high-quality digital learning. It aims to strengthen digital competencies among students and teachers and support the integration of advanced technologies across the Valencian education system. The available description does not specify particular AI tools, teaching methods, or learning activities.
pedagogicalSummary: The inspected strategic-plans page describes a 2024–2028 digital education roadmap, but does not explain teaching methods, learning activities, or how instruction is organised or supported. It mentions strengthening digital competencies among the educational community, including students and teachers, without specifying a pedagogical model. The related educational-technology landing page lists strategic plans, projects, and good-practice resources, but the inspected material does not establish a particular approach such as project-based, collaborative, or inquiry learning. This is a lack of accessible evidence about pedagogy, not evidence that no such activities exist. Sources: https://ceice.gva.es/es/web/educacion/innovacio-tecnologica-educativa/plans-estrategics and https://ceice.gva.es/es/web/educacion/innovacio-tecnologica-educativa
prioritySummary: The initiative’s stated emphasis is transforming and modernising the Valencian education system for the digital era. The plan presents digital education that is inclusive, accessible, and high quality as a benefit for all students and teachers, and aims to strengthen digital competencies so the educational community can meet future digital challenges. The page also frames the plan as aligned with international and national initiatives and regulations. It does not identify a narrower priority, such as workforce upskilling or individual well-being, or rank the stated aims against one another. Sources: https://ceice.gva.es/es/web/educacion/innovacio-tecnologica-educativa/plans-estrategics
educationalTechnologySummary: The plan page says that transforming education will involve integrating “advanced technologies” and strengthening digital competencies, but it does not name any technology, platform, software, or hardware, nor explain how a specific tool supports learning. The related projects page identifies administrative units responsible for educational IT projects, but the accessible text does not describe particular tools or their instructional use. Thus, the inspected evidence supports a general commitment to technology integration, not identification of educational technologies developed or used for AI-literacy learning. The pages inspected do not establish whether such technologies are described in the linked strategic plan document or elsewhere; this is a limit of the available evidence, not confirmation that none exist. Sources: https://ceice.gva.es/es/web/educacion/innovacio-tecnologica-educativa/plans-estrategics and https://ceice.gva.es/es/web/educacion/innovacio-tecnologica-educativa/projectes

inclusion.reason: This initiative is issued by a sub-national government (Generalitat Valenciana's Ministry of Education), which qualifies under the inclusion route requiring government endorsement. The site covers AI and advanced technology integration in education as part of official strategic plans for schools. While specific AI literacy content may require further exploration on detailed pages, the government origin and scope across multiple schools make it eligible for inclusion per the inclusive screening criteria.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: ValgrAI – AI tools in Valencian/Catalan
metadata.Description: ValgrAI – Valencian Graduate School and Research Network of AI.

summary: ValgrAI is a Valencian nonprofit foundation and AI education and research network connecting universities, researchers and industry. Its educational offer includes university-linked postgraduate study and microcredentials, specialist courses, teacher professional development and customized training for organizations. Courses cover technical topics such as NLP, as well as generative AI, practical workplace use, ethics, regulation and AI evaluation. Digital-IA adds accessible training for residents of eligible municipalities. Learning is offered online and in person, with practical activities and guided use of AI tools; some programs also include lectures, labs and mentoring.
pedagogicalSummary: ValgrAI’s accessible pages describe a mix of flexible online instruction and in-person workshops. Its Quick Learning courses are self-paced and fully online, while Digital-IA also offers in-person sessions adapted to the group. The stated teaching approach emphasizes practical application: organizational courses combine theory with real-world applications, and workshops include guided practice, experimentation with accessible tools, and activities such as creating digital projects. Some courses explicitly include critical or ethical reflection, including teacher training that involves redesigning classroom activities. The AI Evaluation Programme adds a more structured hybrid format of lectures, labs, mentoring, activities, and an in-person capstone. These descriptions support applied, flexible learning, but detailed methods are not available for every course inspected. Sources: https://valgrai.eu/formacion/ ; https://valgrai.eu/formacion-a-medida/ ; https://digitalia.valgrai.eu/cursos-presenciales/ ; https://valgrai.eu/ai-evaluation-programme/
prioritySummary: ValgrAI’s overall emphasis is developing AI knowledge and talent through postgraduate, specialist, and professional education, while connecting universities and researchers with companies and regional economic needs. Its courses serve both individuals—including students and professionals—and organizations seeking workforce skills and practical AI capabilities. Digital-IA adds an access and inclusion emphasis: it targets residents of eligible smaller municipalities in the Valencian Community, offers free training for people of different ages and prior experience, and includes groups such as older people, immigrants, people with disabilities, and rural workers. Its stated benefits span daily-life autonomy, ethical participation, employability, and business productivity. The inspected pages therefore indicate economic and workforce goals alongside broader access and individual benefit, without establishing one as the sole priority. Sources: https://valgrai.eu/ ; https://valgrai.eu/sobre-valgrai/ ; https://digitalia.valgrai.eu/ ; https://digitalia.valgrai.eu/cursos-presenciales/
educationalTechnologySummary: Digital-IA offers online courses through a linked ValgrAI Campus portal with login and registration; the inspected pages do not identify the platform’s underlying software. ValgrAI also describes online and synchronous online course delivery, alongside in-person teaching. Course descriptions identify tools and environments used in learning activities, including ChatGPT and other AI tools, Microsoft Copilot, Scratch with AI, and Minecraft-based activities. Digital-IA workshops also describe practical experimentation with generative tools for text, images, audio, and video. These are presented as technologies learners use or explore, not as products developed by ValgrAI. Although ValgrAI’s navigation lists software and patents, the pages inspected do not establish specific educational software or hardware that it develops. Sources: https://digitalia.valgrai.eu/ ; https://digitalia.valgrai.eu/cursos-presenciales/ ; https://valgrai.eu/formacion/ ; https://campus.valgrai.eu/login/index.php

inclusion.reason: The initiative meets the AI-literacy requirement through its extensive curriculum of courses and microcredentials focused on AI concepts (e.g., ethics, generative models). It satisfies an inclusion route via explicit government endorsement/funding, evidenced by a stated agreement between ValgrAI and the Generalitat de Catalunya (Conselleria d’Innovació, Universitats, Ciència i Societat Digital), which is a sub-national statutory body. URL: https://valgrai.eu/

metadata.Initiative / Programme: AI in Grade 8+ ICT curriculum (Sri Lanka, 2024)
metadata.Description: Pilot launched March 2024 in 20 schools across all nine provinces, revising the ICT syllabus to add AI content from Grade 8, developed with Sri Lanka's National Institute of Education and Microsoft.

summary: Sri Lanka’s Ministry of Education and National Institute of Education, in partnership with Microsoft, launched a pilot to add artificial intelligence to Information Technology studies for students above Grade 8. The pilot covers 20 schools across the country, with Microsoft staff supporting online educational activities and technical resources planned for delivery. The available report does not specify teaching methods, assessments, or further curriculum details.
pedagogicalSummary: The inspected report describes a pilot integrating AI into Information Technology education for students above Grade 8, with Microsoft staff supporting online educational activities. It does not explain lesson formats, teaching methods, student projects, assessment, or teacher preparation, so no more specific pedagogy can be established from this evidence. The report mentions plans for suitable classrooms and technical equipment, which concern delivery conditions rather than a stated teaching approach. (https://www.newswire.lk/2024/03/20/sri-lanka-partners-with-microsoft-to-introduce-artificial-intelligence-into-school-education/)
prioritySummary: The initiative’s stated emphasis is introducing AI into school education, specifically by giving students above Grade 8 the opportunity to study AI within Information Technology. The report describes a pilot in 20 selected schools across 20 districts and says full implementation was aimed for 2025. It also presents the programme as part of Sri Lanka’s advancement through new technologies, but gives little detail about intended learning outcomes or wider societal benefits; the clearest evidenced beneficiaries are school students. (https://www.newswire.lk/2024/03/20/sri-lanka-partners-with-microsoft-to-introduce-artificial-intelligence-into-school-education/)
educationalTechnologySummary: The report identifies no named learning platform, software, AI application, or hardware. It says Microsoft staff would support online educational activities and that the pilot would provide suitable classrooms and necessary technical equipment, without specifying the equipment or how it would be used for learning. Thus, the accessible evidence points to online delivery support and planned technical resources, but does not establish that the initiative develops or uses any particular educational technology.
